japanese: 冷たぃ…
english: It's cold...

japanese: あれ、なんだろう？
english: Huh? What's that?

japanese: うわ！ なんだこりゃ？
english: Whoa! What is this thing?

japanese: 叔父にスイカ泥棒を教えるべき？
english: Should I tell Uncle about the melon thief?

japanese: 萌の部屋に入れないのはなぜ？
english: Why can't I go in Moe's room?

japanese: 近所の子供たちがいる場所は？
english: Where do the local kids hang out?

japanese: 蜂の巣が怖くて先へ進めない…
english: The beehive is too scary to get past...

japanese: 橋がなくて先に進めない場所が…
english: There's no bridge, so I can't go on...

japanese: 虫相撲に勝つためには？
english: How do I win at bug sumo?

japanese: 夏休み中の過ごし方は？
english: How should I spend my summer?

japanese: 捕虫網はどうやって使うの？
english: How do I use the bug net?

japanese: 珍しい昆虫が見つかる場所は？
english: Where can I find rare bugs?

japanese: 上手な絵日記の書き方は？
english: How do I write a good picture diary?

japanese: 一番眺めの良い場所はどこ？
english: Where's the best view around here?

japanese: 海で泳ぐにはどうすればいいの？
english: How can I go swimming in the sea?

japanese: 運勢を良くするには？
english: How can I improve my luck?

japanese: 夜、おしっこに行くのが怖い…
english: I'm scared to go pee at night...

japanese: え？ スイカ泥棒！ || まったく、悪いことをするやつがいるもんだ || …ところで叔父さんって誰のことだい？
english: What? A watermelon thief! || Honestly, some people have no shame. || ...By the way, which uncle do you mean?

japanese: うーん若い女性は潔癖症というか || なかなか難しいところがあるからね || …ところで萌ってうちの中学の、空野萌のことかい？
english: Hmm. Young ladies can be awfully particular. || They're not easy to figure out. || ...Wait, by Moe, do you mean Moe Sorano from our junior high?

japanese: 子供がたちが集まる場所といえば秘密基地のことかい？
english: A place where kids gather... You mean the secret base?

japanese: なになにそれはたいへんだな || 何か長いものでつついてみたらどうだろう || うーん、たとえば釣り竿とか…
english: My, my. That is a problem. || Why not try poking it with something long? || Hmm, say... a fishing rod?

japanese: それは近くの木を切り倒して橋を作るしかないな || 斧があればいいんだけど… || たとえば物置は調べてみたかい？
english: Then you'll just have to chop down a nearby tree and make a bridge. || If only you had an axe... || Have you looked in the shed, for instance?

japanese: なんだキミも虫相撲をやっているのか || 勝つためには試合開始直前に、土俵の上で虫の背中をつつくこと || とにかく何度かしつこくつついてみるんだ || そうすると虫が興奮して技が出やすくなる || これが、先生直伝のウルトラつんつん必勝法だ
english: Oh, so you're into bug sumo too? || To win, tap your bug on the back in the ring right before the match starts. || Just keep at it. Tap, tap, tap. || That fires the bug up, so it pulls off its moves more easily. || That's my own secret technique: the Ultra Poke-Poke Sure-Win Method.

japanese: キミがもしうちの中学の生徒だったら || 毎晩深夜まで勉強しろ！一学期の復習をわすれるな！ || なーんて言いたいところだけれど || まだ小学生だしな…
english: If you were a student at my junior high, || I'd say: Study till midnight every night! Don't forget to review first term! || ...Or something like that. || But you're still in elementary school, after all...

japanese: 虫網は家の中では使えないけど || でも、家の外に出て虫網を装備すればいつでも使えるはずだ || 試しにやってみるがいい
english: You can't use the bug net inside the house. || But step outside and equip it, and you can use it anytime. || Go on, give it a try.

japanese: なになに… || うんうんそれはちょうどこの裏手の方にたくさんいるな || 山の奥深いところに入っていく秘密の抜け道があるんだ
english: Let's see, let's see... || Ah, yes. There are plenty of those right around the back of here. || There's a secret shortcut that leads deep into the mountains.

japanese: 絵日記にはその日の出来事の中で || もっとも印象深かったことを書くんだ || でも、なーんにも大きな出来事が起こらなかったからといって || がっかりしちゃいけないよ
english: In a picture diary, out of everything that happened that day, || you write about what left the biggest impression. || But even if nothing big happened at all, || you mustn't be disappointed.

japanese: この辺りで眺めの良いところっていうと || てっぺん山のてっぺんだな || でも、あそこの登山口は早い時間に閉まってしまうから || 普通に歩いて間に合うように行くのは || ちょっと難しいかもしれないね
english: The best view around here would be || the very top of Mt. Teppen. || But the trailhead closes early, || so getting there in time on foot || might be a little tricky.

japanese: 海で泳ぎたかったらぼくのなつやすみ２海の冒険篇あれをやりなさい！
english: If you want to swim in the sea, go play Boku no Natsuyasumi 2: Sea Adventure!

japanese: 運を良くする方法？ || それはお地蔵さまにお祈りすることだな || まさにカミダノミ！ || …こらこら、先生が言ったことだからって || なーんでも簡単に信じちゃいけないよ
english: A way to improve your luck? || That would be praying to the Jizo statue. || When in doubt, ask the gods! || ...Now, now. Just because a teacher said it, || you mustn't go believing every little thing.

japanese: それは先生も同じだ
english: That makes two of us.

japanese: ちなみに先生はスイカ泥棒じゃないぞ
english: For the record, I am not the watermelon thief.

japanese: 彼女は私に負けず劣らずがんばり屋さんなんだ || こう見えても先生とは仲がいいんだよ
english: She's every bit as hard a worker as I am. || Believe it or not, she and I get along quite well.

japanese: そういえば高速道路の下に || 子供たちが勝手にものを持ち込んで遊んでいると || 父兄から苦情がきたことがあったな || いいかい、くれぐれもあそこに行っちゃダメだぞ
english: Come to think of it, under the highway... || Kids were hauling things in there and playing without permission, || and we once got a complaint from the parents. || Listen, you must never, ever go there.

japanese: でも危ないから || 釣り竿でつつくのは一日一回だけにしておくんだ || わかったかい
english: But it's dangerous, || so only poke it with the rod once a day. || Understood?

japanese: でも斧は危険だしキミが使うには大きすぎる || 使うのは一日一回だけにしておきなさい || 以上、先生からの忠告だ
english: But an axe is dangerous, and it's too big for you. || Use it only once a day. || That's a word of warning from your teacher.

japanese: 虫相撲か懐かしいなー || 先生も大好きだったよ
english: Bug sumo... That takes me back. || I loved it too, you know.

japanese: 夜になってもうやることがなかったら || 絵日記を書いて早めに寝てしまうことをお勧めするよ
english: If night falls and there's nothing left to do, || I'd suggest writing your picture diary and getting to bed early.

japanese: いいかい || 虫網は必ず、家の外で装備するんだからね
english: Remember, now. || Always equip the bug net outside the house.

japanese: 近所の子供たちとモーレツに仲良くなって || 彼らにその秘密の抜け道を教わることをお勧めするよ
english: I'd suggest making very, very good friends with the local kids || and getting them to show you that secret shortcut.

japanese: なにも大きなできごとがなかった日ほど || しみじみとした味のある絵日記が書けるってもんだ
english: It's the days when nothing big happens || that make for the most heartfelt picture diaries.

japanese: うーん、どこかに || てっぺん山までの近道があればいいんだけど…
english: Hmm. If only there were || a shortcut up Mt. Teppen somewhere...

japanese: あれはねなかなか面白いぞ
english: That one's really quite fun, you know.

japanese: でもお地蔵さまを拝んでいれば || 本当に良いことがあったときお地蔵さまに感謝することになる || 日々の生活の中でそんな気持ちを持つことは || 結構、いいことなんじゃないかな
english: But if you pray to the Jizo, || then when something truly good happens, you'll feel thankful to it. || Carrying that feeling with you day to day || is a pretty fine thing, don't you think?

japanese: でもうちの奥さんはなかなか起きてくれないんだ || いつも困ってる
english: But my wife just won't wake up for me. || It's always a problem.

japanese: こんにちはおひさしぶり
english: Hello there. It's been a while.

japanese: そうだね……
english: Yeah...

japanese: やっとここに戻ってこられたと思ったら || もう秋の気配だ || そうだ、先生がいない間に来ていた || 大学生の研究者には会えたかい？
english: I finally make it back here, || and autumn's already in the air. || Oh, that's right. While I was away, || did you get to meet the university researcher?

japanese: うん、美人さんだったよ / だれのことやねん？ /
english: Yeah, she was really pretty || Who are you talking about?

japanese: …え？…女性だったのか || そいつは知らなかった大後悔だ
english: ...What? ...It was a woman? || I had no idea. I'll regret this forever.

japanese: ここ数年お盆ぐらいから || この山の奥のほうに大学生の研究者が来ているらしいんだ
english: For the past few years, from around Obon, || a university researcher has apparently been coming to the back of these mountains.

japanese: さて、キミからはなにか質問があるかい？
english: Now then, do you have any questions for me?

japanese: こんにちは || 先生の夏休みはそろそろ終わりだ
english: Hello. || My summer vacation is nearly over.

japanese: なんで？
english: How come?

japanese: 毎年、夏休みの後半は || 研修で遠くの街まで行くことになっているんだ || ここ数年、お盆過ぎから || 山の奥のほうに大学生の研究者が来るらしくて || 本当はその人に会ってから行きたいんだけどね
english: Every year, for the second half of summer break, || I have to go to a faraway town for training. || These past few years, after Obon, || a university researcher has apparently been coming up into the mountains. || I'd really like to meet them before I go.

japanese: ふ〜ん、そうなんだ
english: Hmm, I see.

japanese: ところで今日はどんな面白い質問を見つけてきたんだい？
english: So, what interesting question have you found for me today?

japanese: 変なこと言っちゃった || でも、野外研究ってお腹がすくのよね…
english: That came out weird. || But field research really makes you hungry...

japanese: あれ？ こんにちは || 私ヨシコ、よろしくね！
english: Oh? Hello! || I'm Yoshiko. Nice to meet you!

japanese: 今日は教頭せんせの野外研究の助手です || えーと、バームクーヘン？
english: Today I'm the vice principal's field research assistant. || Um... Baumkuchen?

japanese: フィールドワーク
english: Fieldwork.

japanese: それです！
english: That's the one!

japanese: さて、今日もなにか面白い質問があるかな？
english: Now then, any interesting questions again today?

japanese: 今日も暑いね
english: Another hot one today.

japanese: なにしているの？
english: What are you doing?

japanese: もともとこの辺りの野山は、先生にとって思い出深い場所なんだ || だから時間ができるとここに来ていろんなものを観ているんだよ
english: These hills and fields have always held a lot of memories for me. || So whenever I have time, I come here and observe all sorts of things.

japanese: さて、今日もなにか質問があるかな？
english: Now then, any questions again today?

japanese: あれキミはどこの子だい？ || この辺りの子供じゃないな？
english: Hm? And whose boy are you? || You're not from around here, are you?

japanese: ボクはボク
english: I'm Boku.

japanese: そうかよろしくね || こう見えてもおじさんは自然を愛し || 日々、野山でフィールドワークをしている人なんだ || ちなみに鷺の里中学校の教頭先生でもあるよ
english: I see. Pleased to meet you. || I may not look it, but I'm a man who loves nature || and does fieldwork in these hills every day. || I also happen to be the vice principal of Saginosato Junior High.

japanese: え！ 本当！
english: What! Really?

japanese: 疑ってるのかい？ || じゃあなんでもいいから先生に質問してごらん
english: You doubt me? || Then go ahead, ask me anything at all.

japanese: あれ？ おばちゃんだ
english: Huh? It's Auntie.

japanese: フフ…… || ふたりが仲良くしているところを || 写真に撮ろうと思ってここで待ってたのよ
english: Hee hee... || I was waiting here to take a picture || of you two getting along.

japanese: うちのおかあさん、昔東京でカメラマンやってたんだよ… すごいでしょ
english: My mom used to be a photographer in Tokyo... Pretty amazing, huh?

japanese: カメラマン？
english: A photographer?

japanese: でも、助手だったのよ一人前になる前に結婚してここにきちゃったから… || さあさ、二人とも並んだ並んだ
english: Only an assistant, though. I got married and came here before I ever made it on my own... || Come on now, line up, you two.

japanese: はい、おとうさんが好きなのは
english: Okay! What does Dad love most?

japanese: チーズ！
english: Cheese!

japanese: じゃあ、写真が出来たら見せてあげるね || 家に帰ったら柚木さんにも見せてあげるんだよ || きっと喜ぶわ！
english: I'll show you the photo once it's ready. || When you get home, show it to Yuzuki too. || She'll be so happy!

japanese: ゆずきってだ〜れ？
english: Who's Yuzuki?

japanese: うちのおかあさんだよ
english: That's my mom.

japanese: ちゃんといい子にしてたって、おかあさんに教えてあげなきゃね
english: You'll have to tell your mother what a good boy you've been.

japanese: うん
english: Okay.

japanese: じゃあ、二人とも仲良くするのよ
english: Now, you two play nice.

japanese: そろそろ、詩も帰ろうかな || この先は橋が落っこちゃってるし || あっちの方はでっかい蜂の巣があるし || …あんたは、スイカ畑の見張りでもしていてね
english: Guess I'll head home too. || The bridge is out up ahead, || and there's a great big beehive over that way. || ...You just go stand guard over the watermelon patch or something.

japanese: ちょっとだけ楽しかったよじゃあね…
english: That was a tiny bit fun. See ya...

japanese: でも、あんたまでチビ娘って呼んじゃや〜だよ
english: But don't you start calling me Squirt too!

japanese: どうしたの
english: What's wrong?

japanese: し〜っ！し、ず、か、に || 今、ツツドリが托卵しようとしてて || ん……とってもいいところなんだから
english: Shhh! Qui-et-ly, now. || A cuckoo is about to slip its egg into another bird's nest... || Mm... this is the very best part.

japanese: ツツドリはカッコウの親威なんだ || ああ、なんてカワイイしぐさなんだろう…
english: The oriental cuckoo is a relative of the common cuckoo. || Ahh, what an adorable little gesture...

japanese: 『ふと、急に空気が冷たく感じられて、私はその場に立ち止まった…』
english: “All at once the air felt cold, and I stopped where I stood...”

japanese: おひさしぶり
english: Long time no see.

japanese: こんにちは
english: Hello.

japanese: ねぇ、私が高校生になったら || キミんちに遊びに行ってもいいでしょ？
english: Hey, when I'm in high school, || I can come visit you at your place, right?

japanese: うん、いいよ！ / 考えさせてほしい /
english: Sure, okay! || Let me think about it

japanese: え？ 本当！うれしいけど… || ちゃんと考えて言ってるのかな？
english: What? Really? I'm glad, but... || have you actually thought this through?

japanese: なにを？
english: Thought what through?

japanese: こうしてヨシコちゃんは || 現役小学生には色仕掛けが通じないことを || 学んだのであった…
english: And so young Yoshiko learned || that feminine charm does not work || on a real live grade-schooler...

japanese: …なんだそれ
english: ...What's that supposed to mean?

japanese: 宿題のノート…誰に借りようかな？
english: Homework notes... Who should I borrow them from?

japanese: …萌の様子変じゃなかった？
english: ...Has Moe been acting strange?

japanese: うん、落ち込んでるみたい / とっても元気バリバリだよ /
english: Yeah, she seems down || She's full of beans

japanese: …そっか
english: ...I see.

japanese: え〜？ 元気なの？ || もうまったく！ || 親友がこうやってテレパシーの届く距離までわざわざ来て… || 炎天下にアセモ作って見張ってるっていうのに…
english: Whaaat? She's fine? || Oh, for crying out loud! || Her best friend comes all the way out here, right into telepathy range... || and stands watch in the blazing sun getting heat rash...

japanese: なんだそれ？
english: What's that supposed to mean?

japanese: なんだじゃないよ！ || 心から心配しているのよこう、見えてもぉ
english: Don't "what" me! || I'm worried sick about her. Believe it or not.

japanese: どうしたの？
english: What's wrong?

japanese: ふ〜〜 || あることでね私が勝っちゃったみたいなの || 彼女に…
english: Phewww... || It looks like I beat her at a certain something. || Her, of all people...

japanese: おめでとう
english: Congratulations.

japanese: でもちっともうれしくないのよね || ふ… 我ながら困ったもんだ || あ！ ねぇ、見て見て！ヤマメが跳ねた…
english: But I'm not the least bit happy about it. || Hah... I'm hopeless, even to myself. || Oh! Hey, look, look! A trout just jumped...

japanese: え？ どこどこ
english: Huh? Where, where?

japanese: …魚が跳ねる時ってさ || あれ、周りを気にして見てるんだよね
english: ...You know when a fish jumps? || It's taking a good look at what's around it.

japanese: 私、ヨシコ！ || キミが噂の居候で態度がでかくて || 意外に自己主張が激しい困ったちゃんの小学生？
english: I'm Yoshiko! || So you're the freeloader I've heard about? The grade-schooler with the big attitude || who's a surprisingly pushy little handful?

japanese: 萌、今日は留守みたいだね || どこにいったの？
english: Looks like Moe's out today. || Where did she go?

japanese: 鷺の郷に手紙出しに / 山下さんにみりんを買いに /
english: To Saginosato to mail a letter || To Yamashita's to buy mirin

japanese: なーんだ手紙を出しに行ったのか…
english: Oh, she just went to mail a letter...

japanese: マサカ…
english: It can't be...

japanese: へぇ、家のお使いだなんて || なんだか、あの子らしいな
english: Huh, running an errand for the family. || That's just like her, somehow.

japanese: あなた、まさか私にカクシゴトしてないでしょうね？
english: You wouldn't be keeping secrets from me, would you?

japanese: ねぇキミが住んでる街の話を聞かせてよ
english: Hey, tell me about the town where you live.

japanese: なんでって… || 都会の生活に興味があるからだよ || たとえばキミの家の辺りはにぎやかなの？ || うーん、キミの家があるのは何階？
english: Why, you ask... || Because I'm curious about city life. || Like, is it lively around your house? || Hmm, what floor do you live on?

japanese: 一軒家だよ / アパートの二階だよ / マンションの三階だよ /
english: It's a house || Apartment, second floor || Condo, third floor

japanese: なーんだ意外に地味だね建物は田舎とおんなじか…
english: Oh. That's plainer than I thought. So buildings are the same as out here...

japanese: へぇ、庭が無いなんてさっすが大都会！
english: Wow, no yard at all? Now that's the big city!

japanese: 三階！ || へぇ〜 うちの中学の屋上と同じ高さに上がっても || 怒られない街に住んでるなんて || ちょっぴりたっぷりキミのこと見直してしまったよ
english: The third floor! || Wooow. You live in a town where you can go up as high as our school roof || and not get in trouble for it? || I just gained a little bit... no, a whole lot of respect for you.

japanese: にぎやか、といえばここら辺は夜になったらカエルくんがにぎやかなんだ || えへ、春先の話だけどね
english: Speaking of lively, the frogs make quite a racket around here at night. || Heh, in early spring, I mean.

japanese: 雪がとけて春になって || ふもとの鷺の里が田植えで忙しくなるころ… || ここではカエルが鳴き始めるんだ…
english: When the snow melts and spring comes, || and Saginosato down below gets busy with rice planting... || that's when the frogs start singing up here...

japanese: ねぇ、キミって都会から来たの？
english: Hey, are you from the city?

japanese: うん、そうだよ
english: Yeah, I am.

japanese: こーんな田舎に夏休み中ずっといるの？ || タイクツじゃない？
english: You're staying way out here in the sticks all summer? || Aren't you bored?

japanese: なんでって… || じゃ、ここの感想は？
english: Why, you ask... || Well, what do you think of this place?

japanese: やっぱり楽しいよ / ちょっぴり悲しいよ / すっかり腹へった /
english: It's fun, of course || It's a little sad || I'm starving

japanese: そう？ ここって本当になーんにもないと思うけどな
english: Really? I think there's absolutely nothing here.

japanese: そうでしょ！ || とくにこの辺は寂しいもんねすとんと、悲しくなってくるよ…
english: Right? || Especially around here. It's so lonesome the sadness just drops on you...

japanese: なにそれ？ || 居候くん、もしかすると遠慮してご飯食べてるの？
english: What's that about? || Mr. Freeloader, are you holding back at mealtimes?

japanese: いいな、都会っ子か… || 私、大人になったら絶対、大都会に住むんだ
english: Lucky you, a city kid... || When I grow up, I'm going to live in the big city for sure.

japanese: 髪、きれいだねシャンプーなに使ってるの？ || 触っていい？
english: Your hair's so pretty. What shampoo do you use? || Can I touch it?

japanese: あんた、何者？
english: Who are you, anyway?

japanese: 萌の友達だよ、親友！今日はテイサツなの
english: I'm Moe's friend. Her best friend! Today I'm on a scouting mission.

japanese: 親友だからテイサツに来たのよ
english: I'm her best friend, so I came to scout things out.

japanese: そっか、じゃあ萌が彼といっしょに練習するとき || 私も見学させてね || バイバ〜イ
english: I see. Then when Moe practices with him, || let me come and watch too. || Bye-byeee!

japanese: じゃあね
english: See you.

japanese: あーん、まずいよ〜 || 見学させてね、バイバ〜イ！だってさ… || 私ってば、コイガタキの女子にいったい全体、ナニ言ってんだい…
english: Ohhh, this is bad... || "Let me come watch, bye-byeee!" Listen to me... || What on earth am I saying to my rival in love...

japanese: あんたは誰！
english: Who are you?!

japanese: じゃ、あたしはあたし！ || ヨシコちゃん！
english: Well then, I'm me! || Yoshiko!

japanese: ここは、ボロッチだったのをうちのおとうさんがトンカン直したんだよ
english: This place was all run-down, and my dad fixed it up, bang bang bang.

japanese: へぇ、大工さんみたいなんだ
english: Wow, just like a carpenter.

japanese: このちっちゃい川はねユキノ川っていうのよ
english: This little stream is called the Yukino River.

japanese: ふ〜んそうなんだねぇ、ユキって雪？
english: Huh, is it? Hey, is that "yuki" like snow?

japanese: うん、お空から降る雪
english: Yeah, the snow that falls from the sky.

japanese: へぇ、ここは雪が降るところなんだ
english: Oh, so it snows here.

japanese: あんたのとこはちっとも？
english: It doesn't snow where you live? Not at all?

japanese: うん、たまにしかね
english: Nope, only once in a while.

japanese: フフ、可哀相ね || …でも、本当はホタルがポコポコっとたくさん生まれる川だから || ゆきの川って名前になったんだって
english: Hee hee, poor you. || ...But really, it's a river where lots and lots of fireflies pop out, || and that's why it's named the Yukino River.

japanese: え…？ なんでかな？
english: Huh...? How come?

japanese: は？
english: Huh?

japanese: なんで、ホタルがポコポコで、雪って名前になるのかな？
english: Why do fireflies popping out make it get named after snow?

japanese: …そ、それは
english: ...Th-that's...

japanese: ヘエ、知らないんだ
english: Ohh, so you don't know.

japanese: 違うわよ！ || あんたにだけはどんなことがあっても教えちゃいけないって… || おとうさんに絶対、絶対絶対、言われたんだから
english: I do so! || It's just, you're the one person I'm never, ever supposed to tell... || Dad told me absolutely, absolutely, absolutely not to.

japanese: 絶対に秘密なんだから！
english: It's an absolute secret!

japanese: あの子、本当にどこに行ったのかしら？
english: Where on earth has that girl gone?

japanese: 詩… 詩ちゃ〜ん…
english: Shirabe... Shirabeee...

japanese: ねぇ、おばちゃん
english: Hey, Auntie?

japanese: ん…… なあに？
english: Hm...? What is it?

japanese: もしかしたら、詩がいなくなっちゃったのって || ボクが明日、家に帰っちゃうからかなぁ？
english: Maybe Shirabe ran off || because I'm going home tomorrow...?

japanese: うん、そうかもしれないなあの子は一見、気の強い性格のようだけど… || 根はとってもやさしいナイーブな子だから…
english: Yes, that could be. She seems so tough at first glance... || but deep down she's a very gentle, sensitive girl...

japanese: ボク、がんばって探してみるよ
english: I'll do my best to find her.

japanese: そうね、じゃあボクくんは海の方を探してみて… || でも、危ないところには行っちゃだめよ
english: All right. Then you go look down toward the sea, Boku... || But don't go anywhere dangerous.

japanese: うん、わかってるよ
english: Yeah, I know.

japanese: クワやスキ、肥料が置いてあるどこの家の物置なのかな？
english: Hoes, spades and fertilizer. I wonder whose shed this is?

japanese: 小さなお墓がいっぱいなんだかチェスの駒みたい
english: So many little graves. They look kind of like chess pieces.

japanese: うそぉ！なんで負けんだよ！
english: No way! How'd I lose?!

japanese: やっぱズルはいけないね…
english: Guess cheating doesn't pay...

japanese: でも、ガッちゃんボクくんって本当に強くなったね！
english: But Gacchan, Boku's gotten really strong, huh!

japanese: うん、そうだな…
english: Yeah, guess so...

japanese: ちょっと、ついてきないいことを教えてあげるぜ
english: Come with me a sec. I'll show you something good.

japanese: ボクちゃんいいことを教えてやるよ、ここで○ボタンを押してみな！
english: Hey, Boku, I'll let you in on something. Press the ○ button right here!

japanese: え？ 何が起きるの？
english: Huh? What'll happen?

japanese: へへ… オレたち以外は知らない、秘密の抜け道へようこそ！
english: Heh heh... Welcome to the secret shortcut nobody knows but us!

japanese: 秘密の？
english: Secret?

japanese: そう！ ここを通れば龍神池やてっぺん山なんてあっという間なんだぜ
english: Yep! Go through here and you're at Ryujin Pond or Mt. Teppen in no time.

japanese: とにかくボタンを押してみな
english: Just press the button already.

japanese: あれ、ここはいったい…
english: Huh? Where am I...?

japanese: 『私が家に帰る前日、高速道路の下の秘密基地には誰もいなかった… || それは当然、私にとっては寂しいできごとだったのだが || でも、子供は子供の残酷さを承知しているものなので || こういうこともあるさ…と、自分を納得させた』
english: “The day before I went home, there was no one at the secret base under the highway... || Naturally, that was a lonely thing for me. || But children understand the cruelty of children, || and so I told myself: these things happen...”

japanese: 『しかし、池の上を渡ってくる涼風はこの里山での短い夏の時間が || もう、あまり残されていないことを私に感じさせた… || こういうこともあるさ…そう思いながらも || なんだか胸が苦しかった…』
english: “Yet the cool breeze crossing the pond made me feel that my short summer || in these hills had very little time left... || These things happen... Even as I thought it, || my chest ached somehow...”

japanese: すっごくいい天気！ボクくん、こんにちは
english: What gorgeous weather! Hello, Boku.

japanese: うん、おじちゃんおばちゃんこんにちは
english: Hi, Uncle. Hi, Auntie.

japanese: いや〜 しかし今日は空が高いな…
english: My, the sky sure is high today...

japanese: ボクくん、約束通り来てくれてありがとう
english: Thanks for coming like you promised, Boku.

japanese: フフフ、ではボクくん！ || 畑のトウモロコシをかたっぱしからこの籠に入れてね || じゃあ、お仕事スタート！
english: Hee hee. All right, Boku! || Pick every ear of corn in the field and put them in this basket. || Ready... get to work!

japanese: さぁボクくんがんばってね
english: Go on, Boku. Do your best.

japanese: あとかたづけはおじさんたちがやっておくよ || さぁ子供は遊んだ遊んだ
english: We'll take care of the cleanup. || Off you go now. Kids should be out playing.

japanese: ふぅ… でもなんていいお天気なのかしら！うれしいわ！
english: Phew... What lovely weather, though! I'm so glad!

japanese: 明日のお昼にでもおっきなお鍋でたっぷり茹でてあげるからね || 楽しみにしていてちょうだい
english: Around lunchtime tomorrow, I'll boil up a whole bunch in the big pot. || You look forward to that.

japanese: ボクくんこれで、もうそろそろおしまいだね || いやぁ、お疲れ様でした
english: That's just about the last of it, Boku. || Good work out there.

japanese: 私もなんだかいい汗かいちゃったな〜
english: I worked up a nice sweat myself.

japanese: うわぁ、ヘビだぁ！
english: Waah, a snake!

japanese: いやだ、いやだってば
english: No! I said no!

japanese: どうしたんだ！ボクくん、大丈夫か？
english: What happened! Boku, are you all right?

japanese: もう安心だ
english: You're safe now.

japanese: 怖かったのかい？
english: Were you scared?

japanese: そんなことないよ
english: No, I wasn't.

japanese: ははは、男の子はこのくらいで怖がっちゃいけないよ
english: Ha ha ha. A boy shouldn't get scared over a little thing like this.

japanese: 『そこにあったのは、なんだか悲しいくらいに干からびたヘビの抜け殻だった』
english: “What lay there was a snake's shed skin, dried up in a way that seemed almost sad.”

japanese: ヘビの抜け殻を手に入れた
english: Got a shed snakeskin.

japanese: お供え物に真っ黒なアリンコたちがいっぱい！
english: The offerings are crawling with little black ants!

japanese: このお地蔵さまはね
english: This Jizo statue, you see...

japanese: あら？ || あんたといっしょだと最低だわ || これは、占いが出来るお地蔵さまなの || あんたもやってみる？特別に許可するわ
english: Oh? || Being with you gives me the worst luck. || This is a Jizo that can tell your fortune. || Want to try? I'll give you special permission.

japanese: ボク… || お地蔵さまを叩くなんてできないよ
english: I... || I can't hit a Jizo statue.

japanese: じゃあ、あんた私にぶんなぐられたいの？
english: So you'd rather get clobbered by me?

japanese: そんなぁ…
english: Aww, come on...

japanese: お地蔵様ごめんなさい
english: I'm sorry, Mr. Jizo.

japanese: きゃはは、さえないわね || じゃあ、先に行っているよ
english: Kya ha ha, how lame. || Well, I'm going on ahead.

japanese: 砂糖水、落としちゃった
english: I dropped the sugar water.

japanese: 甘いの好きなの？
english: You like sweet stuff?

japanese: うわ！
english: Whoa!

japanese: 『その大きな蜂の巣はグラグラと揺れて… || あと数回、竿でつつくだけで地面に落とせそうな感じだった…』
english: “The big beehive wobbled and swayed... || It felt as if just a few more pokes with the rod would bring it to the ground...”

japanese: やったぁ！
english: I did it!

japanese: なんだろ？
english: What's this?

japanese: あららら……
english: Uh-oh...

japanese: ぎゃあ！
english: Gyaah!

japanese: やっと目が覚めたんだ || 蜂の巣には気をつけなきゃいけないよ || 大事なとこでも刺されたら大変なんだから
english: So you're finally awake. || You have to be careful around beehives. || It'd be awful if you got stung somewhere important.

japanese: なんだ、死んじゃったのかと思ったけど || その様子じゃあまだまだ大丈夫だね！
english: Well, I thought you might've died, || but by the look of you, you'll be just fine!

japanese: 残念だな…ボクくんが気絶している間に || み〜んなでおいしいものでも食べちゃおうと思ったのに
english: What a shame... While you were out cold, || I thought we'd all have ourselves something tasty.

japanese: サナギ…観てきたかい？
english: The chrysalis... Did you go see it?

japanese: ねぇ、観てきた？ || いつのまにか羽化して飛んでいってしまったみたいなんだよね… || あーあ、残念だな
english: Well? Did you see it? || Looks like it hatched and flew off when no one was looking... || Aw, that's too bad.

japanese: でも、いろいろとご協力ありがとう || キミと仲良くなれてちょっぴりうれしかったよ
english: But thanks for all your help. || I was kind of glad we got to be friends.

japanese: え〜とね
english: Ummm...

japanese: も、もしかしたらもう羽化、始まってる？
english: C-could it be hatching already?

japanese: うん！
english: Yeah!

japanese: どうもありがとうご協力に感謝するよ
english: Thank you. I appreciate your help.

japanese: 僕んちは陶芸やってる家なんだ
english: My family makes pottery.

japanese: そうなんだ
english: Oh yeah?

japanese: この辺には多いんだけどね… || 今、本当は家の手伝いをしなくちゃいけない忙しい時期でさ
english: There's a lot of that around here... || Really, it's the busy season and I should be helping out at home.

japanese: うんうん
english: Uh-huh.

japanese: でもどうしても気になるものを見つけちゃったんだ
english: But I found something I just can't stop thinking about.

japanese: 見たい？
english: Want to see?

japanese: ほら、看板の上のほう……
english: Look, up at the top of the sign...

japanese: なんだこりゃ〜
english: What in the world is that?

japanese: サナギたぶん蝶のサナギ || なんだかどうして普通のサイズよりかなり大きめなんだよね
english: A chrysalis. Probably a butterfly's. || And for some reason it's a good deal bigger than normal.

japanese: 明日かあさってかどうやらその辺で羽化する感じかな
english: Tomorrow, or the day after... I'd say it'll hatch around then.

japanese: へぇ、そうなんだ
english: Huh, really?

japanese: というわけで明日から || キミも時々、ここを観に来てくれないかな？
english: So, starting tomorrow, || could you come by and check on it now and then too?

japanese: うん、いいよ！ / そんなのやだよ！ /
english: Sure, okay! || No way!

japanese: そうくると思った
english: I figured you'd say that.

japanese: まあまぁそんなこと言わないで協力してよ
english: Now, now, don't be like that. Help me out.

japanese: もし僕がちょうど目を離している最中に || 羽化が始まりそうになったら || 大急ぎで教えて欲しいんだ
english: If it looks like it's about to hatch || right when I've taken my eyes off it, || I want you to come tell me as fast as you can.

japanese: いいかい明日から時々、観に来てくれよ
english: Remember, come take a look now and then, starting tomorrow.

japanese: 今日はこうやってスイカ泥棒が来ないように見張っているんだ
english: I'm keeping watch today so the watermelon thief doesn't come.

japanese: あぁ、こんな暑い日にこそ冷たいスイカを食べたいな
english: Ahh, a hot day like this is just when you want some cold watermelon.

japanese: 『スイカ泥棒は、いかにも腕っぷしの強そうな地元の子供だった || そして、私のいつもの癖が始まった』
english: “The watermelon thief was a local boy who looked like he could handle himself in a fight. || And then that old habit of mine kicked in.”

japanese: ヒック！
english: Hic!

japanese: 誰かいるのか？
english: Somebody there?

japanese: 『もうだめだ！そう思った時…』
english: “I'm done for! Just as I thought so...”

japanese: ちぇっ！山犬でもおりてきたか…
english: Tch! Did a wild dog come down from the hills...?

japanese: 『その雄たけびは、どこか遠く深い山々の奥の方から || 夏の里山の騒々しさとはまるで不釣り合いに、寂しくそして悲しく響いた…』
english: “The howl rang out from somewhere far off, deep in the mountains, || lonely and sad, utterly out of place in the noisy summer hills...”

japanese: 遅い〜 || レディを待たせるなんて本当にダメな人ね
english: You're laaate. || Keeping a lady waiting. You really are hopeless.

japanese: ごめんなさい…
english: I'm sorry...

japanese: まぁ、詩はとてもやさしい子だから特別に許してあげる
english: Well, Shirabe is a very kind girl, so I'll forgive you just this once.

japanese: この花はね…
english: This flower, you see...

japanese: 中のミツがとっても甘くて美味しいの
english: The nectar inside is really sweet and yummy.

japanese: あっ本当だ、こりゃいいね || ねぇ、なんて花なのこれ？
english: Oh, you're right. This is great! || Hey, what's this flower called?

japanese: たしか… || ムラサキチューチューっていうの
english: I think... || it's called a Purple Slurp-Slurp.

japanese: そうだよ、ニヒヒじゃあ、つぎね
english: That's right. Nee hee hee. Okay, next.

japanese: 詩… お〜い、詩…
english: Shirabe... Heeey, Shirabe...

japanese: あっ！ 詩を見なかったかい？ || 薫が朝から見てないって言うもんだから探しているんだけど…
english: Oh! You haven't seen Shirabe, have you? || Kaoru says she hasn't seen her since this morning, so I'm out looking...

japanese: そういえば、朝ゴハンの後… 縁側で赤いリボンを見つけたよ
english: Come to think of it, after breakfast... I found a red ribbon on the veranda.

japanese: 詩のかな？
english: Shirabe's, you think?

japanese: そうだと思う
english: I think so.

japanese: 無茶をする子じゃないから大丈夫だとは思うけど…
english: She's not a reckless child, so I'm sure she's fine, but...

japanese: この辺りは戦後焼け野原になった東京を復興させるために || 木がたくさん切り出されて一時期、はげ山になっていたんだ
english: After the war, to rebuild a Tokyo that had been burned to the ground, || so many trees were cut around here that for a time these were bare hills.

japanese: 場所によっては森の様子がすっかり変わってしまってね || どこになにがあったのかさっぱりわからなくなった || あれは悲しかったな
english: In places the forest changed completely. || I couldn't tell where anything used to be. || That was a sad thing.

japanese: 戦争に行ったことも辛い思い出だけど || 帰ってきてからもいろいろとたいへんだったんだよ || さて、今日もなにか質問を考えてきたかい？
english: Going off to war is a painful memory too, || but there were plenty of hardships after I came home. || Now then, have you thought up a question for today?

japanese: なんだ… ここから先に行けないじゃないか〜
english: Aw, what...? I can't get any farther this way.

japanese: この木を切って橋を作ればいいのかな？
english: Maybe I could chop down this tree and make a bridge?

japanese: よいしょっ！
english: Heave-ho!

japanese: よいしょっ！ うわっ！
english: Heave-ho! Whoa!

japanese: また明日だなぁ
english: Guess that's it till tomorrow.

japanese: 『そこは、地元の悪ガキどもが普段、たむろしているのだろう || いわゆる秘密基地というやつだった』
english: “It must have been where the local rascals usually hung around. || What you would call a secret base.”

japanese: とにかくお化けみたいにバカでかいヤマメなんだって…
english: Anyway, they say it's a trout so huge it's like a monster...

japanese: ふん、そんなのウソに決まってらぁ
english: Hmph, that's gotta be a lie.

japanese: 夢をみたんだよきっとそうだ！
english: It was a dream. That must be it!

japanese: カビた給食のパンが二個入っている
english: Two moldy school-lunch rolls inside.

japanese: クモ男のライダーカードを発見！でも、水を吸ってぼろぼろだ
english: Found a Spider Man Rider card! But it's soggy and falling apart.

japanese: サンダルが片方だけ入っている
english: Just one sandal inside.

japanese: 丸めた答案用紙を発見
english: Found a crumpled-up test paper.

japanese: アタマのないトンカチが入っている
english: A hammer with no head inside.

japanese: 爆竹を手に入れた！
english: Got some firecrackers!

japanese: 『スイカ泥棒たちが食い散らかしたスイカの残骸だった…』
english: “It was the wreckage of the melons the watermelon thieves had gorged themselves on...”

japanese: あれ？ おまえ誰だよ？
english: Huh? Who're you?

japanese: …スイカ、食べていたのかい？
english: ...Were you eating watermelon?

japanese: うん、これは食い放題なんだ
english: Yep. It's all-you-can-eat.

japanese: おいしい？
english: Is it good?

japanese: 奥沢のじいちゃんちのには負けるけどん〜 まあまあってとこだな || 食うか？ 食うんなら持ってきてやるぞ
english: Not as good as the ones at Gramps's place in Okusawa, but... mm, not bad. || Want some? I'll bring you one if you do.

japanese: じゃあ、いずれもらうよ
english: Maybe some other time.

japanese: 名前は？
english: What's your name?

japanese: …ボクって呼ばれてる || 夏休みだけ、ここの下のおじちゃんちに来ているんだ
english: ...They call me Boku. || I'm staying at my uncle's place down below, just for summer vacation.

japanese: え！ げぇ、やっばいの… || おじちゃんちって、そこの焼き物やっている家だろ？
english: What! Aw, crud... || Your uncle's place... that's the house that does pottery, right?

japanese: うん…
english: Yeah...

japanese: このスイカもね
english: And these watermelons are...

japanese: そうか…
english: I see...

japanese: おまえ、バラすなよ || いいか、男と男の約束だからな破ったら、しっぺ百回ね || 絶対の絶対だぞ！
english: Don't you rat on me. || Got it? This is a promise between men. Break it and it's a hundred wrist flicks. || I mean absolutely, positively!

japanese: うん、わかっているよ
english: Yeah, I know.

japanese: そうか、よっしゃ！
english: All right, then!

japanese: オレの名前はガッツっていうんだ
english: The name's Guts.

japanese: ここは、オレたちの秘密の秘密基地だ || へへ、なかなかいかすだろ
english: This is our secret secret base. || Heh heh, pretty cool, huh?

japanese: 本当は、メンバー以外は入っちゃだめなんだけど
english: Really, nobody's allowed in but members.

japanese: 今後、特別に入場を許可する！
english: But from now on, you get special permission to enter!

japanese: これって、スイカの秘密を知ったから？
english: Is that because I know the watermelon secret?

japanese: へへ、そういうこと
english: Heh heh, you got it.

japanese: ねぇねぇ、じゃあ合い言葉は？
english: Hey, hey, so what's the password?

japanese: え？ なに？
english: Huh? What?

japanese: 基地に入るときの合い言葉はないの？
english: Isn't there a password for getting into the base?

japanese: な〜んだ、それなら…
english: Oh, that. Sure, it's...

japanese: あれぇ… || たいへんだ！忘れちゃったよ
english: Uh... || Oh no! I forgot it!

japanese: ここではみんなカブトムシやクワガタを闘わせたり || 交換して遊んでいるんだ
english: In here we all make our rhino beetles and stag beetles fight, || and trade them and stuff.

japanese: きたきた…
english: Here he comes...

japanese: 都会の腐った風の匂いがするぜ
english: I smell the rotten wind of the city.

japanese: もやしっ子、ちゃんと朝メシ食ってきたか？
english: Hey, beansprout. Did you eat a proper breakfast?

japanese: 紹介するよボクちゃんだ
english: Let me introduce you. This is Boku.

japanese: よろしく…
english: Nice to meet you...

japanese: こっちがマンモスデブ
english: This here's the Mammoth Fatso.

japanese: うるさい！
english: Shut up!

japanese: ファットっていうんだよろしくな
english: He goes by Fat. Be nice to him.

japanese: どういう意味なの
english: What does that mean?

japanese: あのね、鷺の郷で農家の手伝いに来ていた外人のお姉ちゃんが || オレさまを見つめてうっとりして目を潤ませこう言ったのさ
english: Well, see, a foreign lady who'd come to help on a farm in Saginosato || took one look at yours truly, went all dreamy and misty-eyed, and said this:

japanese: オー！ ファット（脂肪）！
english: Ohh! Fat!

japanese: で、意味は？
english: So, what does it mean?

japanese: こっちはメガネこいつ、あったまいいんだ
english: This one's Specs. He's real smart.

japanese: こんちは、ボクくんキミ、きれいな目をしてるね
english: Hiya, Boku. You have beautiful eyes.

japanese: …はぁ？
english: ...Huh?

japanese: こいつ、ちょっと変なヤツだけど || いじめたらオレが承知しないからな
english: He's kind of a weird one, || but pick on him and you'll answer to me.

japanese: ボクはそんなことしないってば！
english: I'd never do that!

japanese: ねえ、もうそろそろ夏休みもおしまいだけど || ボクくんは、いつ自分ちに帰るの？
english: Say, summer vacation's almost over. || When are you going back home, Boku?

japanese: たぶん、三十一日だと思うけど
english: The thirty-first, I think.

japanese: へへ、さっさと帰ってかあちゃんのおっぱいでも飲むんだな
english: Heh heh, hurry on home and go drink your mama's milk.

japanese: そうか、そうだよな… || いつかは帰らなきゃいけないもんな
english: Right. Yeah, of course... || You've gotta go home sometime.

japanese: 戻って、あっちの友達になめられるんじゃないぞ
english: When you get back, don't let your friends there push you around.

japanese: ハハ、ボクは元々あっちの学校に通ってたんだよ
english: Ha ha, I went to school there in the first place.

japanese: そうだったな…
english: Oh yeah, that's right...

japanese: おまえ、もう少しちゃんと食べて太れよ…
english: You oughta eat a little more and fatten up...

japanese: うん、ちょうどいいくらいにね
english: Sure. Just the right amount.

japanese: ボクくん… もうなんだか長い付き合いみたいな気がするね
english: Boku... It kind of feels like we've known each other a long time already.

japanese: …そうだね
english: ...Yeah, it does.

japanese: 明日、秘密の秘密兵器を投入するぞ！
english: Tomorrow I'm bringing out my secret secret weapon!

japanese: まさか！ ガッちゃんあれはちょっと卑怯だよ
english: No way! Gacchan, that's kinda dirty.

japanese: へへ… 勝負はやったもん勝ちだぜ！
english: Heh heh... Whoever wins, wins!

japanese: 君たち… 勝ち負けじゃなくて、もっと心のゆとりをさぁ…
english: You guys... It's not about winning or losing. Leave a little room in your hearts...

japanese: やだね〜！
english: No thanks!

japanese: フフフフ、ついにオレの秘密兵器が登場だぜ！ || やつと戦ってみたければ虫相撲でキング戦を選んでみな！
english: Heh heh heh, my secret weapon makes its debut at last! || If you want to take him on, pick the King match in bug sumo!

japanese: お、虫相撲のいいカモ来たよん
english: Ooh, here comes an easy mark for bug sumo.

japanese: とにかくそこのテーブルについてみな！ || ルールはやれば自然に判るって
english: Just sit down at that table there! || You'll figure out the rules as you go.

japanese: コーラのヨーヨーってオモチャ屋で替えヒモ売ってないよな
english: They don't sell spare strings for cola yo-yos at the toy store, do they?

japanese: でも、うちの村ってオモチャ屋ないじゃん
english: But our village doesn't even have a toy store.

japanese: なんでみんな本とか、全然読まないの？
english: Why don't any of you ever read books or anything?

japanese: げへへ、だってこれ以上頭が良くなったら || おやじの仕事を継げねえじゃねえか
english: Geh heh heh. 'Cause if I got any smarter, || I couldn't take over my old man's job, could I?

japanese: ねぇ、ヨーヨーのチャンピオンが隣の町まで来ているらしいよ！
english: Hey, I heard the yo-yo champion's come all the way to the next town!

japanese: チャンピオン？なんだ、オレさまのことか
english: Champion? Oh, you mean me.

japanese: 龍神池でキャンプしてるお姉さんって、なかなか面白い人なんだ || 僕もああいうリリカルな大人になりたいなぁ…
english: The lady camping at Ryujin Pond is a pretty interesting person. || I want to grow up to be a lyrical adult like that...

japanese: なに、それ？リリカルって美味しいの？
english: What's that? Is lyrical tasty?

japanese: オレ… たぶん学校卒業したら、都会に出ていくことになるんだ
english: Me... Once I finish school, I'll probably end up moving to the city.

japanese: うちの田んぼ…売っちゃうんだって
english: Our rice fields... They say we're selling them.

japanese: もやしっ子！おまえ、オレさまみたいに太りたくないのかぁ？
english: Hey, beansprout! Don't you wanna be big like yours truly?

japanese: …萌ねえちゃんってさぁたぶん、スリムな人が好みだと思うよ
english: ...I think Moe probably likes slim guys, you know.

japanese: ガハハ！ なんだそりゃ… || そんなのどうせ、オレさまに惚れるまでの気まぐれなのさ
english: Gah ha ha! What's that supposed to be... || That's just a passing fancy till she falls for yours truly.

japanese: 新学期になったらすぐボクくんにお手紙書くよ
english: I'll write you a letter as soon as the new term starts, Boku.

japanese: うん、じゃあボクもちゃんとお返事書くね
english: Okay. Then I'll be sure to write back.

japanese: そうだよな、やっぱ休みが終わったら帰るんだよな…
english: Right. So when vacation's over, you really are going home...

japanese: うん、そりゃそうだよ
english: Yeah, of course I am.

japanese: オレ… いや、なんでもないや
english: I... Nah, never mind.

japanese: え〜 なんなの？
english: Aww, what is it?

japanese: なんでもないって
english: I said never mind.

japanese: なぁ、ボクちゃん都会に帰る前にさ、萌さんに会わせてくんない？
english: Say, Boku. Before you go back to the city, can't you let me meet Moe?

japanese: くんない
english: Can't.

japanese: ボクくんちの赤ちゃんって、もう生まれたの？
english: Has your family's baby been born yet, Boku?

japanese: じゃあ、明日がいいよ明日は星の位置が最高だって占いの本に書いてあったんだ
english: Then tomorrow would be best. My fortune-telling book says the stars are perfectly placed tomorrow.

japanese: ねぇ、今月号の科学の付録見た？
english: Hey, did you see the free gift in this month's Science?

japanese: え、なになに？
english: Huh? What is it?

japanese: え〜！ 知らないの〜月面車だぜ！
english: Whaaat? You don't know? It's a lunar rover!

japanese: スーパーボールでさいろんな色が混じっているやつがあるだろ || オレはあれを認めないね！ || 理由？ そんなもんは必要ね〜よ！
english: You know those superballs with all the colors swirled together? || I refuse to accept those! || Why? I don't need a reason!

japanese: なかよしねずみのぐりとぐら… || 青いのがぐりだっけ？
english: Guri and Gura, the friendly little mice... || Was Guri the blue one?

japanese: 去年、学校の理科室から鉱石標本を盗んできたんだ… || まぁ、ただの鉄鉱石なんだけど、ずしりと重くてキラキラ輝く宝物さ…
english: Last year I swiped a mineral specimen from the school science room... || It's only iron ore, but it's heavy in your hand and it glitters. A real treasure...

japanese: メンコ？ なにそれ？ || こっちじゃパッチって呼んでるんだ || あれに付いてる小さなへこみって、輪ゴムで束ねる為のものなんだぜ || え？ 常識なの…
english: Menko? What's that? || Around here we call them patchi. || Those little dents on them are for bundling them with a rubber band, you know. || Huh? Everybody knows that...?

japanese: 里見八犬伝って玉の名前は全部言えるけど || どうしても順番が怪しいんだよね…
english: In the Hakkenden, I can name every one of the beads, || but I can never quite get the order right...

japanese: ガンバの冒険ってさやっぱりノロイの目が恐すぎるよね…
english: In Gamba's Adventure, Noroi's eyes really are way too scary, huh...

japanese: 萌さんと話をしたことあるの？
english: Have you ever talked to Moe?

japanese: うわぁ！ なんてこったい！
english: Whoa! You've gotta be kidding!

japanese: 同じ家に住んでるんだから当たり前だろ
english: We live in the same house. Of course I have.

japanese: アニメの主人公ってなんで自分の髪型に文句言わないんだろう？ || いや〜 彼らはもっと自分の権利を主張すべきだと思うな
english: Why don't cartoon heroes ever complain about their hairstyles? || Honestly, I think they should stand up for their rights more.

japanese: 先月、学校でさ… || 先生が女子だけ集めてなんかやったんだよね || その間、男子はドッヂボールしていたんだ
english: Last month at school... || the teacher got just the girls together and did something. || The boys played dodgeball the whole time.

japanese: クリームの蓋に当たりが付いているやつ… || あれを、連続三回当てたことがあるんだぜ
english: You know the cream ones with a prize mark under the lid...? || I've won on those three times in a row.

japanese: ナルニア国ものがたりって… どのお話から読んだ？
english: The Chronicles of Narnia... Which book did you read first?

japanese: ボクちゃん、オレはおまえを本当の仲間として認めるぜ
english: Boku, I hereby recognize you as a real member of the gang.

japanese: フフフ、次はガツンとかましてやるぜ
english: Heh heh heh, next time I'm gonna let you have it.

japanese: ライダースナックってかっぱえびせん姉妹品… って書いてあるのに || 全然違う味だったよな
english: Rider Snacks say "a sister product of Kappa Ebisen" on the bag, || but they tasted totally different, huh.

japanese: テレビ番組の名前って不思議じゃない？ だってさ… || たとえば、ロンパールームのロンパーってなんなの？
english: Aren't TV show names strange? I mean... || like, what's the "Romper" in Romper Room?

japanese: オレの一番小さい時の記憶って、すっげぇ不思議なんだぜ || たぶん、テレビかなにかだと思うんだけど… || 大きなヘルメットをかぶった不格好なやつが || 真っ暗な砂漠に旗を持って立っているんだ
english: My very earliest memory is super weird. || I think it was on TV or something... || There's this clumsy-looking guy in a big helmet || standing in a pitch-black desert, holding a flag.

japanese: それって… || アポロのアームストロング船長じゃない？
english: Isn't that... || Captain Armstrong from Apollo?

japanese: ライダーカード何冊持ってる？
english: How many albums of Rider cards you got?
Seven!

japanese: げ〜 なんで
english: Gehh. How come?

japanese: うち… おとうさんが集めていたんだ
english: At my house... my dad was collecting them.

japanese: 僕、昨日生まれて初めてヘビに触ったよ
english: Yesterday I touched a snake for the first time in my life.

japanese: え？ ヘ、ヘビなんて…
english: Huh? A s-snake...?

japanese: ガッちゃんやファットは平気で触れるのに、僕だけ…恐くて触れなかったんだ
english: Gacchan and Fat can touch them no problem. I was the only one... too scared to.

japanese: ボクちゃんって野球、どこ守ってる人？
english: What position do you play in baseball, Boku?

japanese: …ベンチ
english: ...Bench.

japanese: 模型飛行機そっちでもはやっていた？
english: Were model airplanes big where you live too?

japanese: うん！ でも、ボク… || 竹ひご曲げたりニューム管切ったりするのへたくそなんだ…
english: Yeah! But I... || I'm no good at bending the bamboo strips or cutting the aluminum tubes...

japanese: 僕、大きくなったら偉い人になって、この村に大きな図書館を作るんだ
english: When I grow up, I'm going to be somebody important and build a big library in this village.

japanese: 都会には水泳教室ってもんがあるんだって？ || 泳ぎなんて近くの川で勝手に覚えりゃいいのにな…
english: I hear the city has things called swimming schools? || You'd think you could just teach yourself in the nearest river...

japanese: なぁ、萌さんて普段なにを食べているんだ？
english: Hey, what does Moe usually eat?

japanese: …普通にご飯とか
english: ...Rice and stuff, like normal.

japanese: あとは？
english: And what else?

japanese: おい、おまえオレさまに隠し事するつもりじゃねえだろうな？
english: Hey, you're not planning on hiding things from yours truly, are you?

japanese: なにも隠してないよ〜
english: I'm not hiding anything!

japanese: やっぱり問題はさドリトル先生に出てくるアフリカのカメだよ || やつはいったい何万歳なんだ？
english: The real problem is that African turtle in Doctor Dolittle. || How many tens of thousands of years old is that thing?

japanese: ボクちゃんはテレビ何が好き？
english: What do you like on TV, Boku?

japanese: 変身しても大きくならないヤツが好き
english: I like the heroes who don't turn giant when they transform.

japanese: ふ〜ん、ボクちゃんらしいな
english: Hmm. That's just like you.

japanese: ビニールに入った長いアイスって、なんて呼んでいる？ || なぁ〜 名前ないだろ…
english: Those long ice pops in plastic tubes. What do you call them? || See? They don't have a name...

japanese: 絵本のちいさなうさこちゃんって || なんでお口がバッテン印なんだろう？
english: In the picture books, little Miffy... || why is her mouth a little X?

japanese: 例の秘密、おじちゃんに言わなかったんだろうな
english: You didn't tell your uncle our little secret, did you?

japanese: …もちろん
english: ...Of course not.

japanese: もし、約束やぶったら
english: 'Cause if you break your promise...

japanese: しっぺ百回の刑！
english: The penalty is a hundred wrist flicks!

japanese: 何年生なの？
english: What grade are you in?

japanese: 三年生だよ
english: Third grade.

japanese: なんだぁ、オレ五年生
english: Oh. I'm in fifth.

japanese: オレさまは四年
english: Yours truly is in fourth.

japanese: みんな僕より大きいんだ僕、まだ二年生だよ
english: You're all older than me. I'm only in second grade.

japanese: 詩と同じ？
english: Same as Shirabe?

japanese: そうそう、やなヤツ！やなヤツ！ || だってあいつ、僕のこといじめるの日課にしてるんだよ || 本当にやなヤツ！ やなヤツ！
english: Yeah, yeah. She's awful! Awful! || I mean, she picks on me every single day like it's her job. || She's really awful! Awful!

japanese: 今、どこに住んでいるの？
english: Where are you staying right now?

japanese: おじちゃんち…ここのすぐ下の家だよ
english: My uncle's place... the house just down below here.

japanese: え？ それって空野さんじゃん
english: Huh? That's the Soranos'!

japanese: そうかぁ、あそこか
english: Ohh, that place.

japanese: ファットってあそこの中学生が好きなんだよ
english: Fat likes the junior high girl who lives there.

japanese: へ？ 萌ねえちゃん？
english: Huh? Moe?

japanese: この野郎！ || 口から手ぇ突っ込んで裏返しにしてやろうか！
english: Why, you! || I oughta reach down your throat and turn you inside out!

japanese: まぁまぁ、押さえて押さえて
english: Easy, easy. Settle down.

japanese: 萌さんってやっぱ素敵だろ || いいな、あの家にいっしょに住めて… || なぁ、一日だけこっそり交代しないか
english: Moe really is something, huh. || Lucky you, living in the same house... || Hey, wanna secretly swap places for just one day?

japanese: ボクくんって、本とかたくさん読む人？
english: Do you read a lot of books and things, Boku?

japanese: うん、大好きだよ
english: Yeah, I love them.

japanese: よかった… 僕周りの子と話題が合わなくて困ってたんだ
english: Thank goodness... I never have anything to talk about with the kids around here.

japanese: それって、オレたちバカみたい、じゃん！
english: Hey, that makes us sound like dummies!

japanese: 虫相撲は… || まず、土俵から落ちたりスタミナがなくなってひっくり返ったら負けなんだ || で、負けたヤツは今日一日だけ使うの禁止ってわけわかった？ || まぁ、でも負けた虫なんてみんなすぐ、虫交換に出しちゃうんだけどね || だから、欲しい虫が出てきたらとにかく勝って、虫交換に出させることだね
english: In bug sumo... || first off, you lose if your bug falls out of the ring, or runs out of stamina and flips over. || And the loser can't be used for the rest of the day. Got it? || Well, everybody just puts their losing bugs up for trade right away anyhow. || So if a bug you want shows up, just win, and make them put it up for trade.

japanese: 土俵の横にチョークが置いてあるだろ || あれを使ってどんな強さの虫を出して欲しいのか書いておきな || ボクちゃんはまだまだ初心者だから、そっちの望み通りの虫を出してやるぜ || ちなみにオレたちは、虫の種類毎に一番でかくて強いやつをキングって呼んでいるんだ
english: See the chalk by the ring? || Use it to write down how strong a bug you want us to send out. || You're still a beginner, Boku, so we'll send out whatever you ask for. || By the way, the biggest, strongest one of each kind of bug... we call that the King.

japanese: でも、キングをリクエストできるのは一日一試合だけね || だって、どんなに大きな強い虫でも || 数打ちゃ当るで勝負されたら、いつかは絶対負けるだろ
english: But you can only request a King for one match a day. || I mean, no matter how big and strong a bug is, || if you keep throwing bugs at it, it's bound to lose sooner or later.

japanese: 試合の前に、土俵の上で虫の背中を叩いてみな || そうすると虫が怒って強くなるんだ || でも、あんまり叩いたらスタミナが減りすぎて逆効果なんだけどさ
english: Before a match, try tapping your bug on the back in the ring. || It gets mad and gets stronger. || Tap it too much, though, and its stamina drops and it backfires.

japanese: もし、強いクラスのヤツがボクちゃんのに軒並み負けるようになったら || オレたちももっと本気でもっと強いのを見つけてきてやるぜ！
english: If our strong-class bugs start losing to yours across the board, || we'll get serious and go find even stronger ones!

japanese: がはは、虫ってすごいんだぜ！ || 試合が終わったら、もうすぐにスタミナ満タンって感じ
english: Gah ha ha, bugs are amazing! || The second a match is over, it's like their stamina's full again.

japanese: オレさまを見れば判るけど、虫だって、当然でかいやつの方が強いんだ
english: Just look at yours truly. With bugs too, the big ones are stronger, naturally.

japanese: でも、やっぱ一番強いのはカブトムシちゃんかな
english: Still, the strongest of all has gotta be the rhino beetle.

japanese: 虫の相撲も人の相撲と同じで、勝てば勝つほど強くなるんだぜ
english: Bug sumo's the same as people sumo. The more you win, the stronger you get.

japanese: 種類によっちゃぁ土俵際で一発逆転の大技を出すヤツもいるぜ！
english: Some kinds have a big move that can turn the whole match around at the edge of the ring!

japanese: 虫って種類ごとに頑丈でスタミナが減りにくいのとか、いろんな特徴があるんだ || 人間でいうと僕とファットの違いみたいなもんだね

japanese: まだ、私が今のボクくんより小さかった頃… || 家族といっしょに、この辺にハイキングに来たことがあるんだ… || その日、私はいつのまにか迷子になっちゃってさ… || 夕方になって、心細くなって… || 河原の大きな石の上に座って泣いていたんだ… || そしたら、あの声が…

japanese: どんな声？
english: What kind of voice?

english: So the voice saved you?

japanese: …オオカミ娘ってさ
english: ...You know, Wolf Girl...

japanese: 恐かったか？
english: Were you scared?

japanese: ヘビに会って逃げたんだろ？
english: You saw the snake and ran, didn't you?

japanese: 逃げた / へっちゃら /
english: I ran || No big deal

japanese: あはは…
english: Ah ha ha...

english: Got a problem with that? That kind of hurts...

english: ...Heh, sorry. || But you know, a guy who's a bit of a scaredy-cat...

japanese: チュ！
english: Smooch!

japanese: 魅力的ってもんだ
english: ...is all the more charming.

japanese: じゃあ笑わないでよ
english: Then don't laugh at me.

japanese: 自然に対して、何も恐れを抱かないやつに限って || まるで中性洗剤で洗ったように人間味の感じられないニュータウンを作ったり… || 要はバランスの問題だけど…
english: It's always the ones with no fear of nature at all || who go and build new towns with no human warmth, like they've been scrubbed with dish soap... || It all comes down to balance, though...

english: ...Not quite. || Oh, right... I kissed a grade-schooler, so now I have to marry him.

japanese: 『その時、私は考えた || あの、なにやら不思議なヘンテコお化けを || どうにかして沙織の機械まで誘い出す手段はないだろうか？』
english: “That was when I began to think. || That strange, mysterious Weirdo Monster... || Was there some way to lure it to Saori's machine?”

japanese: 『そう… 私は知っていたのだ || あの、ヘンテコお化けの好物を…』
english: “Yes... I knew. || I knew the Weirdo Monster's favorite treat...”

japanese: お姉ちゃん、絵描くの好きなんだ
english: You like painting, huh?

japanese: ……うん、好きだよ
english: ......Yeah, I do.

english: Huh? Don't ask me why. That's a tough one. || Hmmm... Painting trains your eye to really see things. || And that leads to knowing yourself... || Besides, taking a long, careful look at something makes your brain happy.

japanese: そうなの？
english: It does?

japanese: ふん、ガキはすぐ、だまされるんだから
english: Hmph. Kids are so easy to fool.

english: Ah... I forgot to go buy the paints I've run out of.

english: Huh?

english: Tomorrow I'm heading down the mountain and back to the university.

へ〜 寂しいの？
english: Ohh? Gonna miss me?

english: ...Well...

english: I won't miss you at all, not a bit, not one teeny tiny speck, noooot at all! || I'll miss you less than I'd miss an ant's tonsils!

english: Oh, is that right. Sure, sure...

english: A big stack of books steeped in the smell of campfire smoke.

english: Found a little leftover coffee in the bottom of a pot.

english: “The sign read... || For your safety, please begin your climb by 11 a.m. || ...That was what it said.”

japanese: 『それは、登山者たちがひとつひとつ丁寧に積んでいったものだった』
english: “Climbers had stacked them there with care, one stone at a time.”

japanese: ふあ〜
english: Fwaaah...

english: “At the very top of Mt. Teppen, for some reason, I wanted to take this view I had worked a little to earn || and look at it carefully, carefully, gently, gently, || from one end to the other, so it would stay with me...”

japanese: 『手前の森の梢をかすめた向こう側に… || まず、叔父の家とその庭の柿の木が || 夏の日差しをあびてほのかに揺らめいている姿があり… || さらにその先の、山の稜線が幾分おだやかになったあたりには || 鷺の郷の家々の赤瓦の屋根が見えた…』
english: “Just past the treetops of the nearest woods... || first there was my uncle's house and the persimmon tree in its garden, || shimmering faintly in the summer sun... || And farther on, where the ridgeline grew a little gentler, || I could see the red-tiled roofs of the houses of Saginosato...”

japanese: 『そして丘の西側には周囲の森に抱かれるように || まっすぐに伸びた一本の高速道路があり… || その道が指し示す遠方には生気溢れる八月の海がキラキラと輝いていた…』
english: “To the west of the hill, cradled by the surrounding forest, || a single highway ran straight as an arrow... || and far off where that road pointed, the August sea glittered, brimming with life...”

english: “This hole seems to lead somewhere... || That was what I thought.”

english: What will you read? || Rare Insect Guide || Fun Kite Encyclopedia

japanese: 砂糖を見つけた
english: Found some sugar.

japanese: 砂糖水を手に入れた
english: Got sugar water.

japanese: もう、私決めたの！ || 私は高校にも大学にも行かないで、一生ここで暮らすって…
english: I've made up my mind! || I'm not going to high school or college. I'm going to live here my whole life...

japanese: じゃぁ、高校を卒業してから月夜野に戻ってくればいいじゃない || 鷺の郷にだって仕事はいっぱいあるんだから
english: Then why not come back to Tsukiyono after you finish high school? || There's plenty of work in Saginosato, too.

japanese: なんだか… 正直言ってもう自信ないの！ || 自信とかやる気とか希望とか全然ない… || …おとうさん、よく、人は自分の想いのままに生きていける || 想いの強さがあれば思った通りの自分になれるって言ってたじゃない || 失敗を続ける人はそんな自分が好きなんだし || 悩みつづける人は悩むことが好きなんだ… || だから、強い自分を信じて生きていけば、人は本当に強くなれる || どんな想いでも、いつかは実現させられるって
english: It's just... honestly, I have no confidence anymore! || No confidence, no drive, no hope, nothing... || ...Dad, you always said people can live just the way they wish, || that if you wish hard enough you can become the person you want to be. || That people who keep failing like themselves that way, || and people who keep worrying like to worry... || So if you believe in a strong self and live by it, you really can become strong. || That any wish at all can come true someday.

japanese: だからって、萌はおとうさんのことを嘘つきだとは思わないだろう？
english: But that doesn't make you think your father's a liar, does it, Moe?

japanese: 思うわけないじゃない！ || でもね… 追い続けた夢が意外に簡単に壊れてしまうこともあるんだなって… || 壊れてしまった後はなんだか、悲しすぎてさ… || あのね！息をしているだけでゆううつで関節が痛くなったり…
english: Of course it doesn't! || But... sometimes a dream you've been chasing breaks so easily... || And once it's broken, it's just... too sad... || You know? Just breathing makes me gloomy, and my joints ache...

english: Hm? Now that stings a little.

english: It's just, everything I'm agonizing over... in your grown-up world, || the answers were all worked out ages ago, weren't they?

japanese: うん、それに… || 学歴なんて社会に出て行くためにどうしても必要なものではないし || 萌のような子は上の学校に進まなくても、自然に教養を身に付けることができると思うよ || ただし、今の萌が考えていることを、萌自身がもう少し整理するための時間を持たなければ || きっと、後悔するような結果になってしまうんじゃないかな
english: Mm. And besides... || schooling isn't something you absolutely need to make your way in the world. || A girl like you, Moe, will pick up an education naturally even without going on to higher school. || But unless you give yourself a little more time to sort out what you're thinking now, || I'm afraid you'll end up with something you regret.

english: But you two aren't being fair.

english: And what don't you like?

english: Hmm. So he tries too hard.

english: Sigh... A reply really ought to have come by now...

english: A reply to what?

english: Eh heh heh... Now, what could it be?

english: Don't tell me... Did I write the address wrong?

english: I wonder if I could ride the swing too.

japanese: 重いからに決まってるじゃない
english: Because I'm heavy, obviously.

english: Huh? What? What did you say?

japanese: なんで、ブランコ乗れないの？
english: Why can't you ride the swing?

japanese: それは秘密なのだ
english: That is a secret.

japanese: あ〜あ、まったくほんとになんで全然こないんだろう
english: Sigh... Honestly, really, why hasn't it come at all?

japanese: なにが？
english: Why hasn't what?

english: If there's no reply by the end of tomorrow, maybe I'll be brave and try calling...

english: I'm a coward, so I'm too scared to go in there.

japanese: いやぁ、昨日の夜受験勉強してたらさ… || なんつ〜か、本格的に居眠りしちゃって、教科書ぐちゃぐちゃ
english: Well, I was studying for exams last night, and... || how do I put it... I fell dead asleep, and my textbook's a mess.

japanese: よだれで
english: From the drool.

japanese: 新学期になって、成績悪くなかったら || もうちょっとマイペースで勉強しようかな
english: If my grades aren't bad when the new term starts, || maybe I'll study at my own pace a little more.

english: Oh? What's this?

japanese: これ… あなあなぼぼん
english: This is... ana-ana-bobon.

english: What's that? || Oh, there's an English dictionary in here, and... a tattered letter.

english: Dum-my. This is English. Eng-lish!

english: Can you read English?

english: Of course I can't. It's the class with my least favorite teacher.

english: Let me try reading the letter.

english: Yeah, read it to me, read it to me.

english: Aw, nuts...

english: ...Are you doing this on purpose?

english: Huh? What? Whaaat? Doing what?

english: Yeah. I think they're going to be my treasure.

japanese: そうか…

english: Moe, I found something mysterious in the cave.

english: Are you packing to go home already?

japanese: 全然… だってボクが持ってきたの、ちっちゃなカバン一個だけだもん
english: Not at all... All I brought was one little bag.

japanese: …なんだ、だから毎日おんなじ服を着てたんだ
english: ...Oh, so that's why you wore the same clothes every day.

japanese: 書き損じの手紙がたくさん入っている
english: Full of letters that were started and thrown away.

japanese: シールがぺたぺたと貼られた赤いランドセルがおいてある
english: A red school backpack plastered with stickers.

japanese: 『それは黄色い可憐な花を用いたとっても可愛らしい作りかけの押し花だった』
english: “It was a darling little half-finished pressed-flower piece, made with dainty yellow blossoms.”

japanese: おねえちゃんどうしたの？
english: Moe, what's wrong?

japanese: どこか痛いの
english: Does something hurt?

japanese: ごめんね、私、今さ…
english: I'm sorry. Right now, I...

japanese: …くぅ
ひとりにしておいて…
english: Leave me alone...

japanese: おねえちゃん、大丈夫？
english: Moe, are you okay?

japanese: …うん、大丈夫だよ
english: ...Yeah, I'm okay.

japanese: おばちゃんが、女の子はみんなそうなんだって言ってたよ…
english: Auntie said all girls get like that...

japanese: どこが悪くなったの
english: What part of you got sick?

japanese: なんだか、自分の夢とか希望とか… || もろもろの将来のことが、もうどうでも良くなったって感じ
english: It's like, my dreams, my hopes... || everything about my future... I just don't care anymore.

japanese: もう、ほっといてってばぁ…
english: Just leave me beee...

japanese: 私の前世って、たぶんナメクジだったんだ || それともミミズかなにかかなぁ… || あっ！ 波間を静かに漂うクラゲってのも… || なかなか絶望的でお似合いだなぁ…
english: I bet I was a slug in a past life. || Or maybe an earthworm or something... || Oh! A jellyfish drifting quietly on the waves... || That's nice and hopeless. It'd suit me...

japanese: 今の私に足りないものはいったいなんなんだろ？
english: What on earth is it that I'm missing right now?

japanese: …栄養
english: ...Nutrition.

japanese: あ〜あ、ほんとになんにもやる気がしないなぁ || ここで寝たま〜んまでなんでもできるといいのになぁ…
english: Sigh... I really don't feel like doing anything. || I wish I could do everything while lying right here...

japanese: あ〜あ… なんか誰でもいいから私を元気にして欲しいな
english: Sigh... I wish somebody, anybody, would cheer me up.

japanese: 最近、昼間眠くてさ || おねえちゃん、夜型になっちゃったのかな
english: I've been so sleepy in the daytime lately. || Maybe I've turned into a night owl.

japanese: ヨルガータ？
english: A nye-towl?

japanese: 夜行性ってことだよ || フクロウさんとかコウモリくん… || ムササビさんとかモモンガちゃんもそうだね
english: It means nocturnal. || Like Mr. Owl and Mr. Bat... || And Mr. Musasabi and little Miss Momonga, too.

japanese: でも、ムササビさんとモモンガちゃんの違いは聞かないでね
english: But don't ask me the difference between a musasabi and a momonga.

japanese: ねぇ、不思議な話なんだけどさ || あの、教頭先生がこの辺の山中に宝物を隠したって話… || おねえちゃん、なんだか気になってしょうがないんだよね…
english: Say, here's a strange story. || You know how they say the vice principal hid a treasure in the mountains around here...? || I just can't get it out of my head...

japanese: いったいどこに隠したんだろう？ || この辺の山中に、いかにも宝物を隠しましたって場所はないからなぁ…
english: Where on earth could he have hidden it? || There's no spot in these mountains that just screams "treasure hidden here"...

japanese: 朝方まで勉強してたんだ…
english: I was up studying till dawn...

japanese: だから、もう少し横になってたいんだな
english: So I want to lie here a little longer.

japanese: おねえちゃんてもしかしたら寝ているの大好きでしょ…
english: You really love sleeping, don't you...

japanese: うん、時間があったら毎日、十五時間くらいは寝てたいんだけどね…
english: Yeah. If I had the time, I'd sleep about fifteen hours a day...

japanese: おかあさん！ 詩、帰ってきたよ！
english: Mom! Shirabe's back!

japanese: ボクくん、この辺の池や川で釣りをする時は || 水に落っこちないように気をつけるんだよ || この辺はほとんど釣り人が入っていないからものすごい数の魚がいるんだ || 水がきれいで魚が良く見える時は || 魚の動きを見て合わせのタイミングをとるといいよ || あまり良く見えないところでは目印に軽い浮きをつけると良いかもしれないな || でも、魚からボクくん自身が目立っちゃいけないよ
english: Boku, when you fish in the ponds and rivers around here, || be careful not to fall in the water. || Hardly any anglers come here, so there's a tremendous number of fish. || When the water's clear and you can see the fish well, || watch how they move to time your strike. || Where you can't see so well, a light float as a marker might help. || But don't let the fish get a good look at you.

japanese: いいかい || 直接魚の動きを見て合わせのタイミングを取るか || あまり良く見えないときは軽い浮きを目印につけるんだよ
english: Remember: || either watch the fish directly to time your strike, || or when you can't see well, put on a light float as a marker.

japanese: おじちゃんとおばちゃんは何年前の今日結婚したの？
english: How many years ago today did you and Auntie get married?

japanese: 十七年前だよ || 本当は昨日の予定だったんだけど || 日曜日で杉並区役所がお休みだったのさ
english: Seventeen years ago. || It was supposed to be the day before, actually, || but that was a Sunday and the Suginami ward office was closed.

japanese: そうかぁ、もう十七年もたったのか…
english: I see... It's been seventeen years already...

japanese: ボクくん、縁側のある家に住むのは初めてかい？
english: Boku, is this your first time living in a house with a veranda?

japanese: この家ならどこにいても涼しい、気持ちの良い風が入ってくるだろう… || だから一応、扇風機はあるんだけど、あんまり使ったことないんだよね
english: Wherever you are in this house, you get a nice cool breeze... || So we do have an electric fan, but we've hardly ever used it.

japanese: うん、昔の家は、みんなこんな感じだったんだよ || 周りの地面がみんなコンクリートで埋められちゃってると || たぶん、こういうわけにはいかないんだろうなぁ…
english: Yes, houses in the old days were all like this. || When the ground all around has been buried in concrete, || I suppose it just doesn't work the same...

japanese: 天井、高くていいだろ
english: Nice high ceilings, aren't they?

japanese: おじさんはこの時間になったらいつも、もう、仕事やめて家に帰ってきてるんだ || でも、工房の鍵は夕飯の直前まで開いているから || おじさんのいない時にあそこに入っちゃだめだからね
english: By this hour I've always knocked off work and come home. || But the workshop stays unlocked until just before dinner, || so you're not to go in there when I'm not around.

japanese: 今日は、ちゃんと朝顔に水をやってくれたみたいでご苦労様でした || 明日からも忘れないでお願いします
english: Looks like you watered the morning glories today. Good work. || Please don't forget tomorrow, either.

japanese: おじさんちの畑は自分のところで食べるのに || ちょうど良い広さしか作っていないんだ || 何事も楽チンなのが一番だよ
english: Our field is only as big || as we need to feed ourselves. || Taking it easy is the best way with everything.

japanese: 今日は畑のお手伝いご苦労さまでした || おじさんちの畑は狭いから || ボクくんに手伝ってもらうにはちょうど良いかもしれないなぁ
english: Thanks for helping in the field today. || Our field's small, || so it might be just right for you to help with, Boku.

japanese: 村の寄り合い行くの面倒くさいなぁ… || ボクくん、おじさんの代わりに行ってくるかい？
english: What a bother, going to the village meeting... || Boku, want to go in my place?

japanese: だめよ！ そんなこと言ってボクくんになまけ癖が移ったら || 怒られるのは私なんだから…
english: Stop that! If you talk like that and your laziness rubs off on Boku, || I'm the one who'll get scolded...

japanese: この谷から外に出かけるのって何日ぶりだっけなぁ…
english: How many days has it been since I left this valley, I wonder...

japanese: あ〜あ、しんどかったなぁ || 今日、おじさん一日中、スイカ畑で見張り番していたんだ || でも、おかげ様で本日の被害はゼロだったよ
english: Phew, what a slog. || I stood guard in the watermelon patch all day today. || But thanks to that, today's damages came to zero.

japanese: 今日の見張り番は本当に疲れたな… || でも、こんな日に限ってスイカ泥棒が出て来ないんだもんなぁ…
english: Guard duty really wore me out today... || And of course, it's on a day like this that the watermelon thief doesn't show...

japanese: いや〜 しかし畑の見張り番は今日一日でや〜めた || だって、大変なんだもんいや、本当…
english: Whew... Well, one day of guarding the field and I quit. || I mean, it's hard work. No, really...

japanese: ボクくん、もうそろそろこの家にも慣れてきたかい？
english: Boku, are you about used to this house by now?

japanese: そうなんだ… || この家は元々明治の中頃に建てられた金沢の方の民家なんだって || おじさんの前に住んでいた人が買い取って、ここに移築したんだよ
english: I see... || They say this house was originally a farmhouse built over Kanazawa way in the middle of the Meiji era. || The fellow who lived here before me bought it and had it relocated here.

japanese: イチクって？
english: Relo-what?

japanese: 建物ごと引越しをすることなんだ || なんだかまるでヤドカリみたいだね
english: It means moving house, building and all. || A bit like a hermit crab, isn't it?

japanese: う〜ん、今日はなかなかいい風が入ってくるなぁ
english: Mmm, there's a fine breeze coming in today.

japanese: そういえばそろそろ花火大会だな… || あれ？ 何日だっけな？
english: Come to think of it, the fireworks show is coming up... || Hm? What day was it again?

japanese: 麓の花火大会はボクくんの部屋からの眺めが一番すばらしいんだよ
english: The fireworks down in the village look best of all from your room, Boku.

japanese: あれ？ やっぱり花火大会って昨日だったんだ || そういえば…あいつも鷺の郷の花火大会大好きだったよな
english: Huh? So the fireworks show was yesterday after all. || Come to think of it... he loved the Saginosato fireworks too, didn't he.

japanese: あ〜あ、花火大会見たかったなぁ
english: Aww, I wanted to see the fireworks.

japanese: 薫、ビール！
english: Kaoru, beer!

japanese: ガスコンロの掃除をしてくれたら考えてもいいわ
english: Clean the gas stove and I'll think about it.

japanese: よ〜し、念力でビールをここに…
english: All riiight. By the power of my mind, a beer shall come to me...

japanese: ふわぁ… 余計にノドが乾いてきたなぁ
english: Fwaah... That only made me thirstier.

japanese: 月末の窯の火入れまでにもう少し薪を割っておきたいな || さっさと新しい斧を買ってきて納屋にしまった古いのを処分しちゃわなきゃ…
english: I'd like to split a bit more firewood before we fire the kiln at the end of the month. || I'd better hurry up and buy a new axe and get rid of the old one in the shed...

japanese: そういえば納屋にしまっておいた斧がなくなってるんだよね || まさか、月の輪グマがやってきて持っていったわけじゃないし
english: Come to think of it, the axe I put in the shed has gone missing. || It's not as if a moon bear came by and carried it off...

japanese: ん… 風鈴いい音だな… いい風だな…
english: Mm... That wind chime sounds nice... Nice breeze...

japanese: ケン坊、あいかわらず幸せそうだな… || 今年は山猿軍団やってこなかったもんなぁ
english: Kenbo looks as happy as ever... || The mountain monkey gang never showed up this year, after all.

japanese: ここにお猿さんたちが来るの？
english: Monkeys come here?

japanese: そりゃそうだよ、ここ山奥なんだもん || 猿たちは、二、三年くらいの周期でここらの谷を回って暮らしてるんだよ || でも、畑の被害はいつもイノシシの方が深刻なんだ
english: Of course they do. We're deep in the mountains. || The monkeys make the rounds of these valleys every two or three years. || But it's always the wild boars that do the worst damage to the fields.

japanese: さっき気づいたんだけどケン坊… ハゲてないか？
english: I just noticed... Is Kenbo going bald?

japanese: ケン坊はおじさんたちが東京に住んでいた時から飼っていたんだよ || だから、もうそろそろおじいちゃんなんだ || お年寄りには親切にしなくっちゃね
english: We've had Kenbo since we were living in Tokyo. || So he's getting to be an old man by now. || We have to be kind to the elderly.

japanese: ボクくん最近釣りの調子はどうだい？
english: Boku, how's the fishing been lately?

japanese: ばつぐん / いまいち /
english: Fantastic || Not so hot

japanese: 特にヤマメは、早め早めに合わせるといいんだよ || あの魚は餌がニセモノだってことを一瞬で判断して吐き出すんだ || だから、まだ針をくわえる前に合わせちゃうくらいでちょうどいいんだって
english: With trout especially, strike early. Earlier than you think. || That fish can tell in an instant the bait's a fake, and it spits it out. || So striking before it's even got the hook in its mouth is about right, they say.

japanese: でも、この辺の川は釣り人がほとんど入っていないから || 魚が人間に馴れていなくて本当に釣りやすいよ
english: But hardly any anglers come to the rivers here, || so the fish aren't used to people and they're really easy to catch.

japanese: 今夜は蒸すなぁ…
english: Muggy tonight...

japanese: そろそろ扇風機ぐらい出してこようかな
english: Maybe it's time I got the fan out, at least.

japanese: あれ、今頃うちのノラが鳴いてる… || どうしたんだろうなぁ？
english: Hm? Our Nora's mooing at this hour... || I wonder what's the matter.

japanese: ノラって、あの牛の名前？
english: Nora... Is that the cow's name?

japanese: そうだよ
english: That's right.

japanese: なんでノラなの？
english: Why Nora?

japanese: 野良牛だったからノラっていうんだ || それにしても変だなぁオオカミでも来たのかな
english: She was a stray, a "nora" cow, so we call her Nora. || Still, that's odd. Did a wolf come around or something?

japanese: ノラは、ある日突然うちの門前にいたんだ || そして結局、持ち主が分からなくて || そのまま我が家のノラになったってわけ
english: One day Nora was just there, standing at our front gate. || In the end we never found out who she belonged to, || and so she became our Nora.

japanese: おじさんも、おおかみ娘のテントの辺りまで散歩してこようかな
english: Maybe I'll take a stroll out toward the Wolf Girl's tent myself.

japanese: 明日、床屋さんに行ってこようっと
english: Think I'll go to the barber's tomorrow.

japanese: 今日、床屋さんで聞いた話なんだけど || うちのスイカがなかなかいけるって、麓で評判になってるんだって
english: Here's something I heard at the barber's today. || Word's gotten around down in the village that our watermelons are pretty tasty.

japanese: 特に子供たちの間で評判らしいよ || 自家用だから、どこにも売ってない筈なのになぁ
english: They're especially popular with the kids, apparently. || Funny. We grow them for ourselves, so they shouldn't be on sale anywhere...

japanese: 女の子の心理って男には判らないもんなぁ
english: A man can never figure out what goes on in a girl's head.

japanese: なんのお話？
english: What are you talking about?

japanese: 思春期の娘を持った悩める父親のお話…
english: The story of a troubled father with an adolescent daughter...

japanese: しゅしんき？
english: Adda-lessons?

japanese: ししゅんき
english: Adolescence.

japanese: おじさんたちの思春期なんて、まだ日本がえらく貧しかった頃のことなんだよ
english: When my generation were adolescents, Japan was still a terribly poor country.

japanese: ふぅ……
english: Phew......

japanese: ボクくんの歳なら || まだ、おとうさんやおかあさんって完璧な存在だろう？
english: At your age, Boku, || your father and mother still seem perfect, don't they?

japanese: 意味、良く判んないよ
english: I don't really get what you mean.

japanese: おじさんにとっての両親っていうのは… || 少なくともおじさんが三十歳を過ぎるまで || 人間的な欠陥とか、大きなまやかしなんかを見つけることが出来なかった || ある意味、完璧に近い存在だったんだ… || でも、今度はおじさんが親をやる番になったら || なんと十五の娘に正面突破されちゃったってわけ…
english: For me, my parents were... || at least until I was past thirty, || people in whom I couldn't find any human failing or any great pretense. || In a sense, they were close to perfect... || But now that it's my turn to be the parent, || my fifteen-year-old daughter has gone and broken straight through my lines...

japanese: …負けちゃったの
english: ...Did you lose?

japanese: そうかもしれないなぁ… || でも、親なんていつの時代でもこんなものなのかな
english: Maybe I did... || But perhaps parents have been like this in every age.

japanese: 今日は縁側を吹き抜ける風まで、なんだか中途半端だなぁ…
english: Even the breeze through the veranda feels half-hearted today...

japanese: 薫、ビール…や〜め、やっぱりいらない
english: Kaoru, beer... Never mind. I don't want one after all.

japanese: なんだか最近、寝不足だなぁ…
english: I haven't been getting enough sleep lately...

japanese: そろそろ、登り窯に火をいれなきゃなぁ
english: It's about time I fired up the climbing kiln.

japanese: え？ いついつ？
english: Huh? When, when?

japanese: そろそろ…
english: Soon...

japanese: 登り窯…夏は暑いんだよな
english: The climbing kiln... It's hot work in summer.

japanese: 明日、窯に火を入れるよ
english: I'm firing the kiln tomorrow.

japanese: え！ 本当？
english: What! Really?

japanese: うん！ || ボクくんがここにいる間にやっぱり一度すごいところを見せてあげなきゃね
english: Yep! || I've got to show you the real thing at least once while you're here, Boku.

japanese: 夜中もずっと窯の番をしなくちゃいけないのだけど || ボクくん、いっしょに夜更かしをしちゃだめだよ
english: I'll have to watch the kiln all through the night, || but you're not to stay up late with me, Boku.

japanese: こおろぎの鳴き音に揺れし 我窯のまだ細き火に 我子抱かれん || そうか、こんなことじゃあ僕もまだまだ器が小さいな…
english: Swaying to the song of crickets, in my kiln's still-slender flame, my child is held. || Hmm. If that's the best I can do, I'm still a small vessel myself...

japanese: テレビ、なにやっているんだっけ？
english: What's on TV, again?

japanese: もう、肌にあたるのは秋の風だなぁ
english: That's an autumn wind on my skin already.

japanese: 秋風か… なんだか悲しいなぁ
english: The autumn wind... It makes me a little sad.

japanese: 最近、なんだか夕方になると、寂しいような悲しいような || 不思議な気もちになるんだよね…
english: Lately, when evening comes, I get this strange feeling, || sort of lonely, sort of sad...

japanese: そういえば、戦争が終わった年も… || なんだか、こんな夏の終わり方だったかもしれないな…
english: Come to think of it, the year the war ended... || summer may have gone out just like this...

japanese: おねえちゃんどうしたの？
english: Moe, what's wrong?

japanese: 人生色々だな〜 とかガツ〜ンとか…
english: Oh, you know, "life's full of ups and downs," and "wham," and so on...

japanese: 意味不明
english: Makes no sense.

japanese: とりあえず読みます」
english: Anyway, I'll read it.

japanese: なにそれ？
english: Read what?

japanese: 詩、うるさ〜い || 読むよ…
english: Shirabe, hush! || Here goes...

japanese: 春、大河の流れ咲き誇る花々の香り… || 今、マークトウェインの冒険小説で読んだ夢の国アメリカと || 私の生まれた国…この愛すべき祖国、日本は戦争をしています || トムソーヤハックルベリーフィン || 彼らが遊んだ野山に吹いている風を、日差しを… || 私はいつか自分の肌で感じてみたかった… || 今日まで、密かに、そしてひたむきに彼らの言葉を学んできた私ですが… || それも、そろそろ限界のようです || 英語の辞書もここに隠さなければいけなくなりました || もし、この戦争が終わってまだ、私が生きのびていたならば || 今の、清水のようなこの無垢の志しを… || そして、春の到来を告げる南風のような高揚感を… || 未来の自分へ伝えたいと思います    昭和十七年、春…
english: Spring. The flow of the great river, the scent of flowers in full bloom... || Today America, the dreamland I read about in Mark Twain's adventure novels, || and the country of my birth... my beloved homeland, Japan... are at war. || Tom Sawyer. Huckleberry Finn. || The wind and the sunlight on the hills and fields where they played... || I wanted to feel them on my own skin someday... || Until today I have studied their language, in secret and with all my heart... || but it seems I can go no further. || Now I must hide even my English dictionary here. || If this war ends and I am still alive, || this pure resolve of mine, clear as spring water... || and this elation, like the south wind that tells of spring's arrival... || I wish to pass on to my future self. Spring, Showa 17...
