japanese: ボクくん、二階の机の上にいいものが置いてあるよ
english: Boku, there's something nice waiting on the desk upstairs.

japanese: 二階の机の上にいいもの？
english: Something nice on the desk upstairs?

japanese: そう、見ておいで
english: That's right. Go and see.

japanese: そういえば最近、またまたスイカ泥棒がひどくてね || このまま今より悪くなったら見張りが必要かもしれないな
english: By the way, the watermelon thieving's gotten bad again lately. || If it gets any worse, we may need to post a guard.

japanese: ボクくんも何か見たら教えて下さいね
english: If you see anything, Boku, do let me know.

japanese: 『この時、私はあの秘密基地での一件を… || なぜか叔父には言わなかった』
english: “For some reason, I did not tell my uncle then || about what had happened at the secret base.”

japanese: いやあ、今晩も暑いね
english: Whew, another hot one tonight.

japanese: じゃあ、かき氷でも作りましょうか
english: Shall I make us some shaved ice, then?

japanese: かき氷のシロップは何が好き？
english: What syrup do you like on your shaved ice?

japanese: メロン / イチゴ / レモン / みぞれ /
english: Melon || Strawberry || Lemon || Plain sugar

japanese: メロン / イチゴ / レモン / みぞれ / 虹色スペシャル /
english: Melon || Strawberry || Lemon || Plain sugar || Rainbow Special

japanese: じゃあ、すぐに作り始めるからね
english: I'll get started right away, then.

japanese: 車の中に萌のぶかぶかジャージがあったから || 冷え込んだら着るっておとうさん言っていたよ
english: Moe's baggy track suit was in the car, || so your father said he'd put it on if it got chilly.

japanese: じゃなくて、おとうさんが無理に着たからぶかぶかになったのよ
english: No, it's baggy BECAUSE Dad squeezed into it.

japanese: 詩のもおとうさん着られるかな？
english: Could Dad fit into Shirabe's too?

japanese: おかあさんなら、多分着られるよ || 半ズボンになっちゃうけどね
english: Mom probably could. || They'd turn into shorts, though.

japanese: 今日、鷺の郷のＢコープで聞いたんだけど || この辺の子供で、古井戸に入って遊んでいる子がいるらしいよ
english: I heard this at the B-Co-op in Saginosato today. || Seems some kid around here has been climbing down into the old well to play.

japanese: まぁ、それは危ないわ
english: My, that's dangerous.

japanese: 捜索願いが出ている子はいないから、事故があったわけではないだろうけど
english: Nobody's been reported missing, so there can't have been an accident, but still.

japanese: ボクくん、近所の子の真似をして || あんまり危ない遊びをしちゃだめよ
english: Boku, don't go copying the neighborhood kids || and playing dangerous games.

japanese: そういえば、今日、鷺の郷に行ったときのお土産があるよ
english: Oh, that reminds me. I brought something back from Saginosato today.

japanese: なにな〜に？
english: What is it, what is it?

japanese: というわけで、この後縁側に集合で〜す！
english: And so, everyone meet on the veranda after this!

japanese: な〜になに？
english: What is it, what?

japanese: フフフ…ボクくん、浴衣着ようか？
english: Hee hee hee... Boku, shall we put you in a yukata?

japanese: 今日もなかなか夏らしいいい形の雲が出てたね
english: We had some fine summery clouds again today.

japanese: …あのね、ちょっと小耳にはさんだんだけど || イワシ雲って…イワシの形しているの？
english: ...Um, I happened to hear something. || Sardine clouds... are they shaped like sardines?

japanese: え？ …それはね
english: Hm? ...Well, you see...

japanese: だったら、ドーナッツやソフトクリーム雲もあるのかな？
english: Then are there doughnut clouds and soft-serve clouds too?

japanese: あんみつは？
english: What about fruit jelly?

japanese: ワッフル！
english: Waffles!

japanese: じゃあボクはクロワッサン！
english: Then I say croissants!

japanese: それなら、ふたりで新しい雲の形を探しに風の岬まで行っておいで
english: In that case, why don't you two go to Cape of Winds and look for new cloud shapes?

japanese: 新しい雲？
english: New clouds?

japanese: 風の岬で
english: At Cape of Winds...

japanese: 最新型の雲！
english: The very latest model of cloud!

japanese: でも、風の岬までは遠いから気をつけてね || できるだけ寄り道しないで行くのよ
english: But it's a long way to Cape of Winds, so be careful. || Try not to stop off anywhere on the way.

japanese: ねえ、おじちゃん… || 自分の目で見たり、耳で聞いたりしたことは全部信じていいことなの？
english: Hey, Uncle... || Is it okay to believe everything you see with your own eyes and hear with your own ears?

japanese: う〜ん、それは難しい質問だぞ、たとえば…
english: Hmmm, that's a tough question. For example...

japanese: なんかいいたとえがあるかな
english: Is there a good example, I wonder?

japanese: フフ… あるある || …たとえば、私は優作がとっても良いおとうさんに見えるときと || もう、ぜんぜんまったくいいかげんでどうしようもない || ただのダメおじさんに見えるときがあるわ
english: Hee hee... There is, there is. || ...For example, sometimes Yusaku looks like a wonderful father to me, || and sometimes he looks like a completely, utterly sloppy, || hopeless, good-for-nothing old man.

japanese: ボク、今日…お化け、見ちゃったんだ
english: Today, I... saw a ghost.

japanese: …あんた、そういうことあんまり言わない方がいいわよ
english: ...You probably shouldn't go around saying things like that.

japanese: あら、私は信じるわよ
english: Oh, I believe you.

japanese: 僕も小さい頃、雪の降る夜に、宇宙人が来たと思っていた…
english: When I was little, one snowy night, I thought aliens had come...

japanese: で、正体は？
english: And what was it really?

japanese: 大人になってから名画座で古いアメリカ映画を見てたらさ || 記憶とまったく同じシーンが出てきた…
english: Years later, as a grown-up, I was watching an old American movie at a revival house, || and there it was. The exact scene from my memory...

japanese: 優作さん、かぁさんお風呂借りにきました
english: Yusaku, Ma, I've come to borrow the bath.

japanese: かぁさん、夜分失礼します
english: Sorry to bother you so late, Ma.

japanese: いいのよ 自分の家だと思って、ゆっくり入っていってね
english: Not at all. Make yourself at home and take your time.

japanese: ありがとうございます
english: Thank you very much.

japanese: あれ？ 初めまして…
english: Oh? Pleased to meet you...

japanese: この子、私のお兄ちゃんの子なんだ、おかあさんが臨月で預かっているの…
english: This is my big brother's boy. His mother's due any day, so we're looking after him...

japanese: …ボ、ボクです
english: ...I-I'm Boku.

japanese: あっ、沙織ですこんばんは！ へへ…かわいこちゃんだね
english: Oh, I'm Saori. Good evening! Heh heh... Aren't you a cutie.

japanese: かわいこちゃん？
english: A cutie?

japanese: へへ、かわいこちゃんだね
english: Heh heh. Aren't you a cutie.

japanese: よぉ、ボクくん、お誕生日席じゃないの、やるぅ！
english: Yo, Boku. Seat of honor at the head of the table? Nice going!

japanese: やるぅ？
english: Nice going?

japanese: なんだか〜 そわそわ〜
english: Somebody's all fiiidgety...

japanese: あのさ
english: Hey.

japanese: なに？ 萌ねえちゃん
english: What is it, Moe?

japanese: いっしょにお風呂入ろ
english: Let's take a bath together.

japanese: …え？ なんで？
english: ...Huh? Why?

japanese: いっしょに入ろ…背中、流してあげるから
english: Come on, let's go in together... I'll wash your back for you.

japanese: おねえちゃん、詩今日はどうもありがとう || プレゼントはおとうさんおかあさんの一生の宝物にするからね
english: Moe, Shirabe, thank you so much for today. || Your father and I will treasure these presents all our lives.

japanese: 宝物かぁ… || 私も一生の宝物なんて言えるものを欲しいな…
english: A treasure... || I'd like something I could call a treasure for life too...

japanese: 萌はまだ十五なんだから || これからいくらでも見つけることができるんじゃないか？
english: You're only fifteen, Moe. || Don't you think you'll find any number of them from here on?

japanese: う〜ん、人生そうあるべきよね…
english: Mmm, that's how life ought to be...

japanese: そういえば、うちの学校のあの、ガンバリ過ぎの教頭せんせ || 戦争中に、なんだか自分の大事な宝物をこの裏山に隠したんだって
english: That reminds me. You know our school's overachieving vice principal? || They say that during the war he hid his own precious treasure in the hills back here.

japanese: え？ なに、ナニなあに…
english: Huh? What, what, whaaat...?

japanese: でも、戦時中の宝物なんて今の詩や萌たちが見たら || たぶん、びっくりするほど粗末なものだと思うけど
english: But a treasure from wartime... if you girls saw it today, || I expect you'd be amazed at how humble it was.

japanese: なんだろう？
english: I wonder what it is.

japanese: ふんどし！
english: A loincloth!

japanese: は〜い、出まーす
english: Comiiing, I'll get it!

japanese: はい空野です… あっ！久保田のおじさん
english: Hello, Sorano residence... Oh! Mr. Kubota!

japanese: …いえいえ、こちらこそいろいろとお世話になってます || えっ、そうなんですか！じゃあボクくんにかわりますね || ボクく〜ん…
english: ...No, no, we're the ones who should be thanking you. || What, really? Then I'll put Boku on. || Bokuuu...

japanese: ねぇボクくん… || おばちゃんちの女の子ってふたりとも、すっごくいい子だと思わない？
english: Say, Boku... || Don't you think both of the girls in this house are really, really good kids?

japanese: おばちゃんさ… あの子たちがこうして近くにいてくれるだけで || ああ、私は生まれてきて良かったな || そして、あの子たちの母親になれて良かったなって || そう、思っちゃうくらい幸せなんだ… || そして、こんな幸せな家庭を作ってくれた、優作のことも大好きなんだ…
english: You know... just having those girls near me like this || makes me think: oh, I'm so glad I was born. || And I'm so glad I got to be their mother. || That's how happy I am... || And I love Yusaku too, for making such a happy home with me...

japanese: この夏休みボクくんにもおばちゃんの幸せ、分けてあげられたかな？
english: I wonder... did I manage to share some of my happiness with you this summer, Boku?

japanese: うん！ / まぁまぁ /
english: Yeah! || So-so

japanese: それは良かったわありがとうボクくん…
english: I'm so glad. Thank you, Boku...

japanese: うふふ、そうかまぁまぁか… || でも、おばちゃんたちはボクくんといっしょにいられてとってもとっても楽しかったわ || こんなに家の中がにぎやかになったのは、かなり久しぶりのことだったのよ…
english: Hee hee, I see. So-so, is it... || But we had so, so much fun having you with us. || It's been a very long time since this house was so lively...

japanese: …ボクってそんなにうるさい子だった？
english: ...Was I that noisy?

japanese: フフ、そんなことないよとってもいい子でした…
english: Hee hee, not at all. You were a very good boy...

japanese: そうなんだ、おばちゃんありがとう！
english: Oh, okay. Thanks, Auntie!

japanese: どういたしまして
english: You're very welcome.

japanese: おじちゃん、カブトムシって何を食べるの？
english: Uncle, what do rhino beetles eat?

japanese: う〜んそうだなとりあえず、甘いものなら何でも好きかな
english: Hmmm, let's see. They like pretty much anything sweet.

japanese: 甘いもの？お菓子も好きなの？
english: Sweet things? They like candy too?

japanese: あはは、いくら甘いものが好きっていっても || シュクリームやワッフルはもったいないでしょ || たとえば砂糖水や、スイカを食べた後の甘い汁なんかを || クヌギやサイカチの木に塗っておいて、朝や夕方見に行ったわ
english: Ah ha ha, no matter how much they like sweets, || cream puffs and waffles would be a waste. || We'd take sugar water, say, or the sweet juice left after eating watermelon, || smear it on a sawtooth oak or a honey locust, and go look in the morning or evening.

japanese: ふ〜ん、砂糖水か… || ねぇ、クヌギの木ってどんな木？
english: Hmm, sugar water... || Hey, what does a sawtooth oak look like?

japanese: 大きな太い木で、表面にでっかいひび割れ模様があるから || 見たらすぐに判ると思うよ
english: It's a big, thick tree with a great cracked pattern all over its bark. || You'll know it the moment you see it.

japanese: はい、ボクくんこれ
english: Here you go, Boku.

japanese: あ、写真できたんだおばちゃんありがとう
english: Oh, the photo's ready. Thanks, Auntie.

japanese: そういえば、とってもとってもとっても大きな魚が || 池でザブンと跳ねてたよ
english: Oh yeah, a really, really, really big fish || jumped in the pond with a great big splash.

japanese: それはきっとあの池の主がボクくんに挨拶しに来たんじゃないかな
english: I'll bet that was the master of the pond coming to say hello to you.

japanese: ねぇ、おじちゃん || あんな大きな魚でもボクが釣ることできるかな？
english: Hey, Uncle. || Could I catch a fish as big as that?

japanese: うーん、とっても大きなテンカラ毛バリを作らなきゃだめだろうね
english: Hmm, you'd have to make a very large tenkara fly.

japanese: どうすればいいの？
english: What should I do?

japanese: う〜んと… || じゃあ、山の中からなにか毛バリの材料になるようなものを見つけておいで || そしたら、おじさんが手製の特大毛バリを作ってあげるよ
english: Let's seeee... || All right, go find something in the mountains that could be made into a fly. || Then I'll tie you an extra-large one by hand.

japanese: 材料ってどんなものがいいの？
english: What kind of stuff would be good?

japanese: う〜ん… たとえばうちのワンちゃん || ケン坊の毛みたいなちょっと固めの鳥の羽とか…
english: Hmmm... Say, a bird feather that's a bit on the stiff side, || like the fur on our doggie Kenbo...

japanese: なんだ、それなら簡単だよ
english: Oh, if that's all, it's easy.

japanese: そう？ じゃあがんばって…
english: Is it? Good luck, then...

japanese: そういえば、ボク海の近くで不思議なものを拾ったんだ
english: Oh yeah, I picked up something mysterious near the sea.

japanese: 不思議なもの？え、いったいどんなものを拾ったの
english: Something mysterious? What on earth did you pick up?

japanese: 教えて、教えて
english: Tell us, tell us.

japanese: 入道雲みたいな形の見たこともない石なんだけど || ボクの足元にいきなり転がってきたんだ
english: It's a stone shaped like a thunderhead, like nothing I've ever seen. || It came rolling up right at my feet.

japanese: あ〜 あれかなあれかな
english: Ahh, could it be? Could it be?

japanese: うん！ おじさんがまだ今のボクくんより小さい頃に || おじいちゃんに教えてもらった話なんだけどさ… || 海岸の岩場なんかでたま〜に見つかる || タコ入道のような不思議な形をした石があるんだ
english: Yes! This is a story my grandfather told me || when I was even smaller than you are now, Boku... || Once in a long while, among the rocks on the shore, || you find a stone with a strange shape, like a bald octopus goblin.

japanese: うんうん、それそれ
english: Yeah, yeah, that's it.

japanese: で、それはね
english: And what that is...

japanese: なんと、クジラさんの耳の骨なんだ
english: ...believe it or not, is a whale's ear bone.

japanese: え？ クジラ！
english: Huh? A whale!

japanese: うん、そうなんだ || クジラさんとかイルカくんとか海に住む哺乳類は || 死んだ後、身体が海底に沈んじゃうんだけど || 耳の骨だけ他の骨とつながっていないから || 最初に身体から離れて海岸に打ち上げられるんだってさ
english: That's right. || When whales and dolphins and other sea mammals die, || their bodies sink to the bottom of the ocean. || But the ear bone isn't joined to any other bone, || so it's the first to come loose and wash up on the shore, they say.

japanese: でも、そんなの見つけられるものなの？
english: But can you really find something like that?

japanese: うん、確率はそんなに高くないのだろうけど || とにかく海岸を歩いて慎重に探してみると || 運が良ければ一日に二個も三個も見つかることがあるんだって || たぶん、進化の過程で陸から海へ戻ったクジラさんたちが || また、この大地が恋しくなって戻って来るのかもしれないね
english: Well, the odds probably aren't very high. || But if you walk the shore and search carefully, || with luck you might find two or even three in a day, I'm told. || The whales went back from land to sea as they evolved... || Maybe they get to missing this earth and come back again.

japanese: ねぇ、今日ボクさぁ || あのアンテナ２本のお山のてっぺんまで行ってきたんだよ
english: Hey, today, you know, || I went all the way to the top of that mountain with the two antennas.

japanese: え？ てっぺん山まで行ってきたんだ… あそこは見晴らしが最高だろ？
english: What? You went up Mt. Teppen...? The view's the best there is, isn't it?

japanese: 私たちもここに来てすぐの頃、あそこに登ったのよ || あの山頂からの眺めを見たとき… || ああ… ここに越してきて良かったって心から思ったわ
english: We climbed it too, soon after we moved here. || When I saw the view from that summit... || Ahh... I thought, from the bottom of my heart, I'm glad we came.

japanese: ん？ なあに
english: Hm? What is it?

japanese: 『まだ、自分の家には帰りたくないな… || なぜか、その一言がどうしても言えなかった』
english: “I don't want to go back to my own house yet... || For some reason, I just couldn't say those few words.”

japanese: …ボクもここに来て良かったなって
english: ...I was thinking I'm glad I came here too.

japanese: フフフ…… ありがと || ボクくんに気に入ってもらえて、うれしいわ
english: Hee hee hee...... Thank you. || I'm so happy you like it here, Boku.

japanese: あんた、いつのまにかすっかりうちの子供ね
english: Before we knew it, you turned into one of the family.

japanese: じゃあ、ボクも詩のお兄ちゃん？
english: Then am I your big brother too, Shirabe?

japanese: やだよ！
english: No way!

japanese: さあ、早くごちそうさましちゃお
english: Come on, let's finish up and say thank you for the meal.

japanese: お風呂に入りますか？ / はい / いいえ /
english: Take a bath? || Yes || No

japanese: あら、誰かしら？ごめんなさい入っていますよ
english: Oh, who's that? Sorry, it's occupied.

japanese: あのさ…
english: Um...

japanese: なあに？
english: What is it?

japanese: おねえちゃん…失恋しちゃったんだ
english: I... got my heart broken.

japanese: わ！
english: Wah!

japanese: 男の子だって…
english: It's a boy...

japanese: やったぁおめでとう
english: Hooray! Congratulations!

japanese: おめでとう！ お兄ちゃん
english: Congratulations, big brother!

japanese: …テレビなにが好き？
english: ...What do you like on TV?

japanese: え？ え〜と
english: Huh? Ummm...

japanese: 女の子が好きそうなやつ…
english: The kind of thing girls like...

japanese: テレビのコントって時々、残酷で面白いわね…
english: TV comedy skits are kind of cruel sometimes. That's what makes them funny...

japanese: もう、おなか空いたな… || さっき食べたばっかなのにな…
english: I'm hungry already... || And I only just ate...

japanese: 食べ物、なにが好き？
english: What food do you like?

japanese: なによ！ レディーが優雅な食後のひとときを楽しんでいるというのにさ
english: Do you mind! A lady is trying to enjoy an elegant moment after her meal.

japanese: だから、詩のことはほっといてってばぁ
english: I told you, leave Shirabe alooone.

japanese: さっき食べたばっかなのにもうお腹すいちゃったなぁ || あ〜あ、給食の春雨サラダが食べたいな…
english: I only just ate and I'm hungry already. || Ahh, I want the glass noodle salad from school lunch...

japanese: なにそれ？
english: What's that?

japanese: …あれ？ 知らないんだ
english: ...Huh? You don't know it?

japanese: 春雨サラダのない給食センターなんて、あんたのところは百年遅れているわね
english: A school lunch kitchen with no glass noodle salad? Your town is a hundred years behind.

japanese: あんたってさぁ
english: You know, you...

japanese: …なんでもない
english: ...Never mind.

japanese: あんた、せっかく詩がいろいろ教えてあげようと思って待ってたのに || 途中からどっかに行っちゃうなんてほんと恩知らずね！
english: Here I was waiting to teach you all sorts of things, || and you wander off halfway. You're such an ingrate!

japanese: まったくなに、考えてるんだか…
english: Honestly, what goes on in that head...

japanese: 今日は、たくさんいっぱい楽しかったでしょ || 今度は、もっと遠くまで連れてってあげるよ…
english: Today was lots and loads of fun, wasn't it? || Next time I'll take you even farther...

japanese: あれ、またお腹すいちゃったなぁ…
english: Huh, I'm hungry again...

japanese: ふ〜ん
english: Hmm.

japanese: 特にこんないいお天気の日にね… || こうしてたっくさんのお洗濯ものを干しているとさ || 空野家の旗をずらっと並べて我が家の主婦力を誇示しているような || 女としては、妙に誇らしい不思議な気持ちになってくるんだ…
english: Especially on a beautiful day like this... || when I hang out loads and loads of laundry like so, || it's like lining up the Sorano family flags to show off this household's housewife power. || As a woman, it gives me an oddly proud, mysterious feeling...

japanese: なんだそりゃ…
english: What's that supposed to mean...?

japanese: フフ、でもボクくんも結婚して… || そしてたくさんのお洗濯ものを干す機会があったら || ちょっとだけわかるかもしれないよ
english: Hee hee. But when you get married, Boku... || and you get the chance to hang out lots of laundry, || you may understand, just a little.

japanese: そうかな？
english: You think?

japanese: ただし、ちゃ〜んと || 奥さんのお手伝いをしてあげられる旦那さんにならないと
english: But only if you become the kind of husband || who properly helps his wife.

japanese: フフ… 一生わからない悲しい人生かもね
english: Hee hee... Otherwise it'll be a sad life of never understanding.

japanese: そういえば、ここに… || 今朝の約束をまだ実行していない人がいるみたいだぞ…
english: Come to think of it, there's someone here... || who doesn't seem to have kept this morning's promise yet...

japanese: そういえば、ボクくん…朝顔当番を忘れないで続けてくれたら || 夏休みが終わって家に帰る前におばちゃんボクくんにプレゼントをあげるね！
english: By the way, Boku... if you keep up your morning glory duty without forgetting, || I'll give you a present before you go home at the end of summer vacation!

japanese: ボクくん！晩ごはんのおかず当てっこしようか？ || もし、当てっこしたかったら夕方台所にいるおばちゃんに話しかけてね
english: Boku! Shall we play Guess the Dinner? || If you want to play, come talk to me in the kitchen in the evening.

japanese: おばちゃん、毎日みんなのごはん作るの楽しみなんだぁ…
english: I look forward to making everyone's meals every day...

japanese: ボクくん、そろそろおかあさんのこと恋しいでしょ || ホームシックになってないかな？
english: Boku, you must be missing your mother about now. || You're not getting homesick, are you?

japanese: ホームシックって？
english: What's homesick?

japanese: あのね、たとえば今までずっとボクくんのそばにいた || ボクくんの大好きな人が今は周りにいないでしょ || ボクくんのおとうさんもおかあさんもね || すると、なんとなく悲しかったり寂しかったりして、こない？
english: Well, for example, the people you love who've always been by your side || aren't around you right now, are they? || Not your father, not your mother. || Doesn't that make you feel a bit sad or lonely?

japanese: あれ？ 寂しくないんだ
english: Oh? You're not lonely?

japanese: なんだぁ、ボクくんてずいぶん大人なんだね
english: Well now. You're quite the grown-up, aren't you, Boku?

japanese: うん、でもボクホームシックの意味が分かったら || ホームシックになってみたくなったよ
english: Yeah, but now that I know what homesick means, || I kind of want to try being homesick.

japanese: …そう、じゃあがんばってね
english: ...I see. Well, good luck with that.

japanese: おばちゃんね… || 若い頃、東京に出て来てすぐにホームシックになったんだ
english: You know... || when I was young and first came to Tokyo, I got homesick right away.

japanese: ボクくん、昨日の夜おじちゃんいなかったのに脱走しなかったんだね
english: Boku, your uncle was out last night, and you still didn't make a break for it.

japanese: 今朝はずいぶんとお寝坊さんだったのね
english: You were quite the sleepyhead this morning.

japanese: ボクくん、おばちゃんになにか隠し事してない？
english: Boku, you're not hiding something from Auntie, are you?

japanese: え？ 何も隠してないと思うけど…
english: Huh? I don't think I'm hiding anything...

japanese: そうかな〜 || 昨日の夜、ホタル沢に行ったでしょ
english: Is that so... || You went to Firefly Creek last night, didn't you?

japanese: ごめんなさい、でも… || でも、どうしてわかったの？
english: I'm sorry, but... || but how did you know?

japanese: フフ…… さっきボク君のシーツを取り替えようとしたら || お布団からお客さんが出てきたんだ || おばちゃん、びっくりして暴れちゃったけど、なんとか捕まえちゃったよ
english: Hee hee...... When I went to change your sheets just now, || a little visitor came out of your futon. || I got such a start I flailed around, but I managed to catch it.

japanese: ホタル？ホタルが出てきたの？
english: A firefly? A firefly came out?

japanese: でも、虫かごの中がいっぱいだったみたいだから || おばちゃん、沢に行って逃がして来ちゃったよ
english: But your bug cage looked full, || so I went down to the creek and let it go.

japanese: え〜 そんな
english: Awww, no way.

japanese: でも、ホタルも朝までボクくんといっしょにいられて || 楽しかったんじゃないのかな…
english: But I think the firefly had fun too, || getting to stay with you until morning...

japanese: さぁ？ どうかしら || 自分の虫かごの中を見て確かめてちょうだい
english: Well? I wonder. || Look in your own bug cage and see for yourself.

japanese: え〜 おばちゃんありがとう
english: Ohh! Thanks, Auntie!

japanese: でも、ホタルって昼間見るとただのカミキリ虫ね
english: Though seen in daylight, a firefly's just a plain old longhorn beetle, isn't it?

japanese: おばちゃんってほとんど毎日お外で洗濯物を干しているのに || なんでそんなに色が白いの？
english: Auntie, you're outside hanging laundry almost every day. || How come your skin's so fair?

japanese: う〜ん、どうしてだろうね？ || ビタミンＣの入った果物をたくさん食べてるからかな || あと時々、色が白くなるようにウグイスの出したフンでお顔を洗ってるんだよ
english: Hmmm, I wonder why. || Maybe because I eat lots of fruit with vitamin C. || And now and then I wash my face with nightingale droppings to keep it fair.

japanese: ウグイスの出したフン？ || 本当にそんな物が世の中にあるんだ… || ウンチ？
english: Nightingale droppings? || There's really such a thing in the world...? || Poop?

japanese: そうよ
english: That's right.

japanese: ウグイスの出したフン…本当にそんなものあるんだ？
english: Nightingale droppings... There's really such a thing?

japanese: そうよ、女の人はみんな知っているわ
english: There is. Every woman knows about it.

japanese: 昨日、鷺の郷で花火大会があったのよ || ボクくんの部屋からなら見えたと思うんだけど || 気づかなかった？
english: There was a fireworks show in Saginosato last night. || I think you could have seen it from your room. || Didn't you notice?

japanese: 昨日の花火とってもきれいだったでしょ || ここの家のお兄ちゃんも鷺の郷の花火大会が大好きだったのよ
english: Weren't last night's fireworks beautiful? || The boy who lived in this house loved the Saginosato fireworks too.

japanese: おばちゃん子供の頃の花火大会って || チビ助だったせいで、前に立っている人の浴衣の柄しか覚えてないんだなぁ
english: At the fireworks shows when I was a child, || I was such a shrimp that all I remember is the yukata pattern of the person standing in front of me.

japanese: 大事な大事な手紙〜
english: A very, very important letterrr...

japanese: ねぇ、その歌、なんの歌？
english: Hey, what song is that?

japanese: え？ フフ…大事な手紙の歌！
english: Hm? Hee hee... The Very Important Letter Song!

japanese: 明日は、もうお墓参りかぁ || ぼくのなつやすみ半分まで行っちゃったね
english: Tomorrow's the grave visit already... || Your summer vacation's half gone, Boku.

japanese: ねぇ、明日ってなんの戦争が終わった日なの？
english: Hey, tomorrow's the day what war ended?

japanese: うん、明日の終戦記念日っていうのはね || おばちゃんが、ちょうど今のボクくんくらいのときに太平洋戦争が終わった日なんだ || おばちゃんは北海道の小樽って港町で育ったんだけど || ある日の朝家の近くの丘に昇ったら || いきなり、港に大きなアメリカの軍艦がたっくさん浮かんでいてね || とってもびっくりしておばちゃん、急いで家の中に隠れちゃった
english: Well, tomorrow's anniversary of the end of the war || is the day the Pacific War ended, when I was just about the age you are now. || I grew up in a port town called Otaru, in Hokkaido. || One morning I climbed the hill near our house, || and all of a sudden there were lots and lots of big American warships floating in the harbor. || I was so startled I ran and hid inside the house.

japanese: アメリカ人に会うのが恐かったの？
english: Were you scared of meeting Americans?

japanese: うん、だってアメリカの兵隊さんに捕まったら || 塩かけて頭からガリガリと食べられちゃうって教わっていたんだもん || でもね、上陸してきたアメリカの兵隊さんが || うちの前の路地で小さなノラ猫を抱き上げて || ミャオ… ミャオ… って言っているのを窓の隙間からこっそりと見てたら || な〜んだ、同じ人間じゃないかって、おばちゃん、そう思ったんだ…
english: Yes. We'd been taught that if the American soldiers caught you, || they'd sprinkle you with salt and crunch you up head first. || But then one of the American soldiers who came ashore || picked up a little stray cat in the alley in front of our house || and went "Meow... meow..." I was peeking through a gap in the window, || and I thought: why, they're people just like us...

japanese: もうあの日から三十年もたったんだね…
english: Thirty years have gone by since that day...

japanese: そうか、今日は結婚記念日だったのか…
english: Oh, so today was our wedding anniversary...

japanese: 完璧に忘れていたわ
english: I completely forgot.

japanese: あ！ 飛行機雲だ
english: Oh! A vapor trail.

japanese: おばちゃん、生まれ変わったら || ジャンボ機のパイロットもやってみたいなぁ
english: If I'm born again, || I'd like to try being a jumbo jet pilot.

japanese: え？ でも… || 普通、女の人はスチュワーデスになりたいんじゃないの？
english: Huh? But... || don't ladies usually want to be stewardesses?

japanese: いや… なるなら断然パイロットだな
english: No... If I'm doing it, it's pilot all the way.

japanese: ねぇボクくん、詩見なかった？ || あの子、さっきからいないのよね… || 心あたりのあるところは片っ端から探したんだけどどうしたのかな…
english: Say, Boku, have you seen Shirabe? || She's been gone for a while now... || I've looked everywhere I can think of. I wonder what's happened...

japanese: もう、そろそろ帰ってくると思うんだけどな
english: I'd think she'd be coming home any time now...

japanese: うちの娘も、すっかりたくましくなったなぁ
english: Our girl's grown up so sturdy.

japanese: やっぱり、親が優秀なんだな
english: It just goes to show, she has excellent parents.

japanese: そろそろ晩ごはんのアイディアも尽きてきたなぁ
english: I'm about out of ideas for dinner.

japanese: そうか！ あれはしばらく作ってなかったなぁ
english: I know! I haven't made that in a while.

japanese: ん〜 || あ〜して… || こ〜して… || よ〜し！ 本日の晩ごはん計画、完成！
english: Mmm... || Do this... || Then that... || There! Tonight's dinner plan is complete!

japanese: そういえば今日から…フフ… 二階の女の子部屋に行ってごらん
english: Oh, that's right. Starting today... hee hee... go have a look in the girls' room upstairs.

japanese: 萌ちゃんがボクくん解禁！ って言っていたわよ || フフ… 何かしらね || 気になるならお部屋に行ってみたら？
english: Moe said, "The ban on Boku is lifted!" || Hee hee... I wonder what's up. || If you're curious, why not go to her room?

japanese: お醤油… 生姜…お砂糖… || …あと、お魚は何にしようかな？
english: Soy sauce... ginger... sugar... || ...Now, which fish shall I use?

japanese: 今日もいい風が吹いてくるわ
english: There's a lovely breeze again today.

japanese: ねぇ、ここの家のお兄ちゃんって、いつ死んじゃったの？
english: Hey, when did the boy who lived here die?

japanese: ……三年前よ
english: ......Three years ago.

japanese: ボクくん、その時麻疹にかかってたから、お葬式来られなかったのよ
english: You were down with rubeola then, Boku, so you couldn't come to the funeral.

japanese: マシーン？
english: Ruby-who?

japanese: …ちょっと違うわ
english: ...Not quite.

japanese: 麻疹って、はしかのことよ
english: Rubeola means the measles.

japanese: ボクくんて、どんな昆虫でもへっちゃらなのかな？
english: Boku, are you fine with any kind of insect?

japanese: うん！ || クモとゴキブリ以外はだいたい大丈夫だよ
english: Yeah! || I'm okay with pretty much anything but spiders and cockroaches.

japanese: そうなんだ、じゃあおばちゃんと同じだね
english: Is that so? Then you're the same as me.

japanese: うん！ あとはどんな虫でも… || 手足をもいだり分解して気持ちが悪くなったことはないよ
english: Yeah! And any other bug... || I've never felt sick pulling off its legs or taking it apart.

japanese: …そういうへっちゃらか
english: ...Oh. That kind of fine.

japanese: 男の子って、虫でもお人形でも、とにかく分解しちゃうんだね
english: Bugs or dolls, boys will take anything apart, won't they?

japanese: あ〜あ、退屈だわ || 詩、蝶々になってお空を飛びたいな…
english: Ahh, I'm so bored. || I want to turn into a butterfly and fly through the sky...

japanese: おばちゃんがパイロットになりたいんだって
english: Auntie says she wants to be a pilot.

japanese: じゃあ、詩はスチュワーデスさんになりたいな
english: Then Shirabe wants to be a stewardess.

japanese: うちの家族って、なんだかみんな高いところが好きみたいなんだ、なんでだろ？
english: Everybody in my family seems to like high places. I wonder why.

japanese: ブランコってこんな山の中だと || なんだか、アルプスの少女ハイジって感じだな
english: A swing, way out here in the mountains... || It's a little like Heidi, Girl of the Alps.

japanese: フフ、さっきおばちゃんもブランコしてきたんだ
english: Hee hee, I had a go on the swing myself just now.

japanese: もっと〜広い世界を見てみたい〜 || わたしは〜 白いコスモス〜
english: I want to seeee more of the wide, wide wooorld... || For I aaam a white cosmos flowerrr...

japanese: それ、なんの歌
english: What song is that?

japanese: えっ？ あ〜 これはおばちゃんのてきとうな鼻歌だよ
english: Hm? Ohh, that's just Auntie humming any old thing through her nose.

japanese: 鼻の歌？
english: A nose song?

japanese: お花の歌！
english: A flower song!

japanese: もっと〜広い世界を見てみたい〜 || わたしは〜 白いコスモス〜
english: I want to seeee more of the wide, wide wooorld... || For I aaam a white cosmos flowerrr...

japanese: おばちゃん… ボク今気づいたんだけど || おばちゃんて、いったいいつお洗濯しているの？
english: Auntie... I just realized something. || When exactly do you do the laundry?

japanese: え？ それはボクくんたちがラジオ体操で目覚める前よ…
english: Hm? Before you all wake up for radio exercises...

japanese: ラジオ体操の前にお洗濯も朝ごはんの支度も || みんな、みんな終わらせているのよ
english: The laundry, getting breakfast ready... || I finish all of it, every bit, before radio exercises.

japanese: あんた、ちょっと見ててあげるから乗ってみなさいよ
english: Go on, get on. I'll watch you for a bit.

japanese: あんたのブランコなかなかうまいじゃない
english: You're not half bad on the swing.

japanese: でも、詩の方が絶対うまいんだから
english: But Shirabe's definitely better.

japanese: こ、こんにちは
english: H-hello.

japanese: …どうも
…遊んでるの
english: ...Are you playing?

japanese: 名前…なんていったっけ？
english: What was... your name again?

japanese: 教えない！
english: Not telling!

japanese: あ… うそ… || 詩って書いてしらべなの
english: Ah... I didn't mean it... || It's written with the character for "poem," and you say it Shirabe.

japanese: よろしくお願いいたしまする
english: I am most pleased to make thy acquaintance.

japanese: こちらこそよろしくお願いいたしまする
english: And I am most pleased to make thine.

japanese: なんか、怒ってない？
english: Are you mad about something?

japanese: あんた、なんでここに来たのよ？
english: What did you come here for, anyway?

japanese: 痛い目にあったって知らないんだから
english: Don't blame me if you get hurt.

japanese: 教えない〜
english: Not telliiing.

japanese: 詩は一人で遊ぶのが好きなんだから、ほっといてちょうだい！
english: Shirabe likes playing by herself, so leave me alone!

japanese: 今日も働きアリたちはせっせ、せっせとがんばって働いているのね || 美しいわ…
english: The worker ants are hard at it again today, bustling, bustling away. || How beautiful...

japanese: 今日は占い地蔵をやってみた？ || 大吉が出るまでがんばって何度も何度もやったら || いくら運の悪いあんたでも今後の人生、ちょっとは良くなるかもね
english: Have you tried the fortune Jizo today? || If you keep at it over and over until you get Great Luck, || even someone as unlucky as you might see life get a little better.

japanese: でも、そうすると…お地蔵さまを何度も殴らなきゃいけないじゃないかぁ
english: But then... I'd have to hit Mr. Jizo over and over...

japanese: あんたが私に殴られるよりはましでしょ
english: Better that than getting hit by me, isn't it?

japanese: 詩ってさ… || アリンコ大好きなんだ
english: You know, Shirabe... || really loves ants.

japanese: アリの世界から、帝王学をまなぶつもりなの
english: I intend to learn the art of ruling from the world of the ants.

japanese: …てーおー？
english: ...Roo-ling?

japanese: そして、輝かしい未来が詩の前には広がっているのよ
english: And a glorious future spreads out before Shirabe.

japanese: 詩は絶対ビッグになるんだから
english: Shirabe's going to be big, no matter what.

japanese: 女王アリって、どんな冠をかぶっているのかしら？
english: What sort of crown does a queen ant wear, I wonder?

japanese: ウグイスのウンチって知っている？
english: Do you know about nightingale poop?

japanese: 知っているわよ || いつも誰かにくっついて行動している人のことでしょ || 詩はなんでも知っているんだから
english: Of course I know. || It's what you call somebody who's always tagging along after someone else. || Shirabe knows everything.

japanese: 女王アリって、どんなドレスを着ているのかしら？
english: What sort of dress does a queen ant wear, I wonder?

japanese: 給食のおかず何が好き？ボク、鯨の竜田揚げ！
english: What's your favorite school lunch dish? Mine's fried whale!

japanese: 詩は… 春雨サラダとカレーシチュー！
english: Shirabe's is... glass noodle salad and curry stew!

japanese: 鯨って硬くてさ || お昼休みが終わってもまだ噛んでることがあるのよね…
english: Whale's so tough, though. || Sometimes I'm still chewing after lunch break is over...

japanese: 給食のソフト麺って油っこくてお腹痛くならない？
english: Don't the soft noodles at school lunch get so greasy they give you a tummy ache?

japanese: え〜 なったことないなぁ
english: Huh? That's never happened to me.

japanese: でもボク、ソフト麺好きなんだ || 三時間目ぐらいから匂いがしてくるんだよね
english: But I like soft noodles. || You can start smelling them from around third period.

japanese: うちの学校… || ソフト麺のときだけパンが小さくなって、減量パンっていうんだよ
english: At our school... || only on soft noodle days the bread gets smaller, and they call it diet bread.

japanese: ねぇ、駄菓子屋ってあんたのとこにもあるの？
english: Hey, do you have a penny candy shop where you live too?

japanese: そりゃあるけどどうしたの？
english: Well, sure. Why?

japanese: ここ… 田舎過ぎて駄菓子屋ないのよね || 私、流行に敏感なのにさぁ
english: This place... is so far out in the sticks there's no candy shop. || And me so sensitive to the latest trends.

japanese: 今日はなんだか血の雨が降る予感がするわ
english: I've got a feeling it's going to rain blood today.

japanese: 血の飴？
english: Blood candy?

japanese: そう、いやな予感がするのよね
english: Yes. I've got a bad feeling about it.

japanese: 誰かに大きな大きな不幸がやってくるのよ！
english: A great, great misfortune is coming to somebody!

japanese: なんで、働きアリさんは文句も言わずに || 毎日毎日、女王アリのために働きつづけるのかしら？
english: Why do the worker ants keep working for the queen, || day after day, without a word of complaint?

japanese: そんなことわかんないよ
english: How should I know?

japanese: へへ… 詩は知ってるんだ
english: Heh heh... Shirabe knows.

japanese: それは女王アリがこの巣の中で、たった一人の女の子だからよ！
english: It's because the queen is the one and only girl in the whole nest!

japanese: エッチ！
english: Pervert!

japanese: へ〜んだ、おまえのかあちゃんで〜べ〜そ
english: Nyah nyah, your mama's got an outie belly button!

japanese: あ！ おかあさんに言いつけてやるんだから
english: Ah! I'm telling Mom on you!

japanese: あっ！ やめておばちゃん怒ったら恐そう…
english: Ah! Don't. Auntie looks scary when she's mad...

japanese: へへ、うちのおかあさんが怒ったら || おとうさんだって納戸に閉じ込められるんだよ
english: Heh heh. When my mom gets mad, || even Dad gets locked in the storeroom.

japanese: そういえば最近…ジャンボさんいないのよね？
english: Come to think of it... Mr. Jumbo hasn't been around lately, has he?

japanese: 誰？ その人
english: Who's that?

japanese: え？ 知らないの！
english: Huh? You don't know?!

japanese: もうまったく、あんたってダメね！ さっさと自分ちに帰っちゃえばいいのに…
english: Honestly, you're hopeless! You should just hurry up and go home...

japanese: え〜とね、ジャンボさんはお魚なの… || ムラサキチューチューのちょっと先に住んでいて詩と仲良しさんなの
english: Ummm, Mr. Jumbo is a fish... || He lives a little past the Purple Slurp-Slurps, and he's Shirabe's good friend.

japanese: 誰かに食べられちゃったのかな？ でもなんで… || いつのまにか、みんなみんないなくなっちゃうのかな…
english: Did somebody eat him? But why... || Why does everybody, everybody, end up going away before you know it...?

japanese: あんた、家に帰る前にちゃんとジャンボさんにご挨拶に行った？
english: Did you go say a proper goodbye to Mr. Jumbo before you go home?

japanese: それって誰？
english: Who's that?

japanese: え？ 知らないの大きなお魚さんなんだけど || あんたここにひと月もいたくせに、そんなことも知らないの？ || まったくあきれた人ね！とっとと自分ちに帰っちゃいなさいよ！ || あの子はね、ムラサキチューチューのちょっと先に住んでいるの… || とってもとっても大きいんだから！
english: Huh? You don't know? He's a great big fish. || You've been here a whole month and you don't even know that? || You're unbelievable! Just hurry up and go home already! || He lives a little past the Purple Slurp-Slurps... || And he's really, really big!

japanese: でもなんで…いつのまにか、みんなみんないなくなっちゃうのかな…
english: But why... Why does everybody, everybody, end up going away before you know it...?

japanese: おおかみ娘ってどんな人？
english: What's the Wolf Girl like?

japanese: う〜ん、あの子ばかりは一言では言い表せないなぁ
english: Hmmm, that girl is the one person I can't sum up in a word.

japanese: あのね… || 育ちが良い好青年みたいな美人のお姉さんなの
english: Let's see... || She's a beautiful young lady who's like a nice, well-brought-up young man.

japanese: …おかま？
english: ...So she's a boy?

japanese: 私ももう少し若かったらまたいろんなことやりたいなぁ…
english: If I were a little younger, I'd love to try all sorts of things again...

japanese: チビ娘っていつも一人で遊んでいるの？
english: Do you always play by yourself, Squirt?

japanese: その呼び方、禁止〜
english: That name is baaanned.

japanese: 友達… いないの？
english: Don't you... have any friends?

japanese: そんなことあるわけないでしょ！ || 詩なんか、友達百人と富士山の上でおにぎり食べられるんだからぁ…
english: Of course I do! || Why, Shirabe could eat rice balls on top of Mt. Fuji with a hundred friends...

japanese: 富士山ってどこにあるんだっけ？
english: Where is Mt. Fuji, again?

japanese: 友達少ないの…
english: So you don't have many friends...

japanese: そうよ、悪かったわね
english: That's right. Sorry about that.

japanese: 知らないよ
english: I don't know.

japanese: 給食の時間に他の子のおかずや、粉末コーヒー取ったりするからかなぁ
english: Maybe it's because I take other kids' food and coffee powder at lunchtime...

japanese: あ〜あ、久しぶりに風の岬に行きたいなぁ
english: Ahh, I want to go to Cape of Winds. It's been so long.

japanese: 夕日がとってもきれいなところ… || でも、途中の橋が落ちてて行けないのよね || あんた！ なんとかしなさいよ
english: The sunset there is so beautiful... || But the bridge on the way is out, so we can't get there. || Hey, you! Do something about it!

japanese: 風の岬って、とってもきれいなとこなんだから
english: Cape of Winds is a really beautiful place, you know.

japanese: 今朝、顔洗ってて気づいたんだけどさ || 釣りって怖くないの？
english: I realized something while I was washing my face this morning. || Isn't fishing scary?

japanese: だって、クジラさんが針にかかったら || いっしょに海まで連れて行かれちゃわない？
english: I mean, if a whale got on your hook, || wouldn't it drag you off to sea with it?

japanese: 今朝、歯を磨いていて気づいたんだけどさ || 凧上げって、実はとっても素敵な遊びなんだね？
english: I realized something while I was brushing my teeth this morning. || Kite flying is actually a wonderful game, isn't it?

japanese: だって〜 もし、凧さんに引っ張られて || そのまま空高く飛んで上がったら、それはとてもとても素敵な体験でしょ
english: I meeean, if the kite pulled you along || and you flew right up high into the sky, that would be a very, very wonderful experience.

japanese: おとうさん、今日はめずらしく仕事してるみたいなの
english: Dad actually seems to be working today, for once.

japanese: 登り窯って、冬はついでにヤキイモ焼くんだよ
english: In winter, they bake sweet potatoes in the climbing kiln while they're at it.

japanese: ねぇ、あのおねえちゃんが読んだ手紙の人、あのあとどうなっちゃったの？
english: Hey, the person in that letter Moe read... What happened to him after that?

japanese: わからないってさ
english: Nobody knows, she says.

japanese: なんだか、カッコ良さそうな人だよね
english: He kind of sounds like a cool guy.

japanese: そう？ でも、今はもうおじいちゃんだよ
english: You think? But he'd be an old grandpa by now.

japanese: 愛があれば歳の差なんか関係ないわ
english: When there's love, age makes no difference.

japanese: ボクくん…ぼくのなつやすみも、あと残り一週間だよ || やりたいことは今のうちにさっさとやっとこうね！
english: Boku... there's only one week left of your summer vacation. || Whatever you want to do, hurry up and do it while you can!

japanese: おばちゃんも一週間くらいでいいから夏休みが欲しいなぁ
english: I wish I could have a summer vacation too, even just a week.

japanese: おばちゃんヨンテンゼロだよ
english: Mine's 20/5, you know.

japanese: 両目の視力…
english: My vision. In both eyes...

japanese: あれ？ 渡り鳥かな…
english: Hm? Migrating birds, maybe...

japanese: いったいあの子、どこに行ったのかしら？ || ねぇ、詩に会わなかった？どっかに行っちゃったみたいなのよね || もう、まったく人騒がせなやつなんだから！
english: Where on earth has that girl gone? || Hey, you haven't seen Shirabe, have you? She seems to have wandered off somewhere. || Honestly, she's such a troublemaker!

japanese: 見つけたらぶん殴ってやるんだから、まったく…
english: When I find her I'm going to wallop her, I swear...

japanese: ふう〜 もうこの斧もそろそろ寿命かな || これは納屋にしまってきて新しいのを使おう
english: Phew... This axe is about at the end of its life. || I'll put it away in the shed and use the new one.

japanese: ふぅ〜 もう少しだがんばるぞ！
english: Phew... Just a little more. Keep at it!

japanese: 土色のお皿や茶碗が、気持ち良さそうに日光浴をしている
english: Clay-colored plates and bowls are happily sunbathing.

japanese: ふぅ、やっと終わった
english: Phew, finally done.

japanese: ご苦労さまでした
english: Good work, Uncle.

japanese: 明日の夜には窯を開けて焼きあがった物を見せてあげるよ
english: Tomorrow night I'll open the kiln and show you how everything came out.

japanese: ふう〜 やっぱりこの快感は何ものにも代え難いな…
english: Phew... There's really no feeling in the world like this one...

japanese: おじちゃん、夜中どうしてたの？
english: Uncle, what did you do all night?

japanese: ずっとここで、薪を割る薪をくべる… の繰り返しだったよ
english: I was right here the whole time. Split wood, feed the fire... over and over.

japanese: 今、なかは何度くらいなの？
english: How hot is it inside right now?

japanese: …目標の七十パーセントって感じかな || とにかく今は、おじさんがんばって薪をくべる速度を速くして || 温度を上げているところなんだ
english: ...About seventy percent of the target, I'd say. || Right now I'm working hard to feed the wood in faster || and bring the temperature up.

japanese: ふぁ〜 でも、久々にやるとやっぱり眠たいなぁ
english: Fwaah... Doing this after so long sure makes me sleepy, though.

japanese: 優作がんばってね！もう少しで久々の現金収入よ！
english: Hang in there, Yusaku! Our first cash income in ages is almost here!

japanese: なんだか私まで疲れてきちゃったな
english: I'm starting to feel worn out myself.

japanese: おじちゃん、がんばって今日から窯焼きするんだって || なんでもちゃんと時間通りに見に行かないと || 面白いところを見逃しちゃうかもしれないから || ボクくんもがんばって何度も見に行ってね…
english: Your uncle's going to do his best and fire the kiln starting today. || If you don't go and look right on time, || you might miss the interesting parts, || so do your best and go see it lots of times, Boku...

japanese: それにしても今年の夏って本当に雨が少ないわ
english: We really have had so little rain this summer.

japanese: 四国のおばあちゃんち水不足で困ってなきゃいいんだけどね
english: I hope Grandma's place in Shikoku isn't suffering from the water shortage.

japanese: 登り窯すると、何日もかけて割っておいた焚き木を || あっという間に使っちゃうんだよ…
english: When they fire the climbing kiln, firewood that took days and days to split || gets used up in no time...

japanese: 詩、男の子に生まれなくて良かったわ || 薪割り、絶対手伝わされてるもん！
english: Shirabe's glad she wasn't born a boy. || I'd have been made to help split wood for sure!

japanese: てっぺん山のアンテナのところって人が住んでいるの？
english: Does somebody live up by the antennas on Mt. Teppen?

japanese: 登り窯の煙… てっぺん山から見えるかな？
english: The smoke from the climbing kiln... I wonder if you can see it from Mt. Teppen.

japanese: 登り窯って、昨日火を消したのに、近づくとまだあったかいんだよ
english: The fire in the climbing kiln went out yesterday, but it's still warm when you get close.

japanese: そういえば、昔、窯の中でかくれんぼしたら || お父さんにすっごく怒られちゃったな…
english: Come to think of it, a long time ago I played hide-and-seek inside the kiln, || and Dad got really, really mad at me...

japanese: 小屋の横に、割られた薪のたばが積まれている
english: Bundles of split firewood are stacked beside the hut.

japanese: たるの中から、お漬物のすっぱい匂いがする
english: A sour smell of pickles comes from the barrel.

japanese: 釣竿を手に入れた
english: Got the fishing rod.

japanese: フジヤマ燃料店と書かれたガスボンベがある
english: A gas cylinder marked "Fujiyama Fuel Co."

japanese: 斧を手に入れた
english: Got the axe.

japanese: なんだか、陸に上がったクジラさんみたい
english: Kind of like a whale that's come up on land.

japanese: ノボリガマさん真っ赤になって怒ってる
english: Mr. Climbing Kiln has turned bright red. He's furious.

japanese: さぁ、もう少しで目標温度だ！
english: Almost at the target temperature now!

japanese: 今は？
english: Where is it now?

japanese: もう、目標の九十パーセント以上かな
english: Over ninety percent of the target, I'd say.

japanese: ふぅ〜 あともう少しだ…
english: Phew... Just a little more...

japanese: やった！ ついに目標の温度まで達したぞ || あとはがんばってこれを二時間持たせればオーケイなんだ！
english: Yes! We've finally reached the target temperature. || Now I just have to hold it there for two hours and we're set!

japanese: よーし、最後のふんばりだがんばるぞ！
english: All riiight, the final push. Let's do this!

japanese: ふ〜 そういえばさっきの雨、一瞬で止んだけどすごい降りだったね
english: Phew... By the way, that rain just now stopped in a flash, but it sure came down hard.

japanese: キミはいつもこの辺、ひとりで来てるの？ || ひとりで川で遊ぶのは危ないよ
english: Do you always come around here by yourself? || It's dangerous to play in the river alone.

japanese: ユキノ川水系は急に増水することがあるんだ
english: The Yukino River system can rise without warning.

japanese: 新しい友達はできたかい？
english: Have you made any new friends?

japanese: うんできたよ！ / いや、まだなんだよね /
english: Yeah, I have! || No, not yet

japanese: そうなんだ… || 僕なんかいまだに一人ぼっちさ
english: I see... || As for me, I'm still all on my own.

japanese: そうかいじゃ僕とおんなじだ
english: Is that so? Then you're the same as me.

japanese: 昔、この川で溺れた子がいたんだ || あいつ、生きてたら今ごろ何してるんだろ？
english: A long time ago, a kid drowned in this river. || If he'd lived, I wonder what he'd be doing now.

japanese: お久しぶり || もう宿題は済んだ？
english: Long time no see. || Finished your homework yet?

japanese: ばっちり完璧！ / かなり絶望的！ /
english: All done, perfect! || Pretty hopeless!

japanese: それはよかった
english: Glad to hear it.

japanese: ま、みんなそんなもんでしょ
english: Well, that's how it is for everybody.

japanese: それよりキミって || もしかするとこの辺の子じゃないのかな？
english: More to the point, || could it be you're not from around here?

japanese: そうか夏休みで来てたのか… || 久しぶりにいい友達ができてうれしかったのに…
english: I see. So you were here for summer vacation... || And I was so happy to make a good friend for the first time in ages...

japanese: じゃ、そろそろ自分の家に帰らなきゃいけないね
english: Then it's about time you went back to your own home.

japanese: 大きな大きなバケツおじさんの仕事に使うのかな？
english: A great big bucket. Does Uncle use it for his work?

japanese: ここで土をこねるらしい
english: This seems to be where the clay gets kneaded.

japanese: あ、そこは危ないからさわっちゃだめ || その棚は作りが悪くてちょっとぐらついているみたいなんだ || 何度も、何度も修理しているんだけどな〜んで落ちちゃうんだろう
english: Ah, don't touch that. It's dangerous. || That shelf's poorly built, and it seems to be a bit wobbly. || I've fixed it again and again. Whyyy does it keep coming down?

japanese: そこ、なんだか夜中のうちに落ちちゃったみたいでさ… || もうちょっと頑丈な筈なんだけどなぁ
english: That seems to have come down sometime in the night... || It ought to be a bit sturdier than that...

japanese: 秘密のうわぐすり… と書かれた大きなバケツ
english: A big bucket labeled "Secret Glaze."

japanese: おじちゃん、毛バリの材料見つけてきたよ
english: Uncle, I found the stuff for the fly.

japanese: どれどれ
english: Let's have a look.

japanese: あれ？ これ…なんだっけ？ || まぁ、いいやちょっとやわらかすぎるけどがんばって作ってみるよ || 二日くらいで完成すると思うから || そしたら、また取りに来て下さいね
english: Hm? This is... what was it again? || Oh well. It's a little too soft, but I'll do my best to make it. || I think it'll be done in two days or so, || so come back for it then.

japanese: ボクくん、例のでっかい毛バリ完成したよ
english: Boku, that great big fly is finished.

japanese: うわぁ、おじちゃんどうもありがとう
english: Wow! Thank you so much, Uncle.

japanese: こんにちは
english: Hello there.

japanese: ボクくん！ここがおじさんの工房だよ || どう？ なかなか面白い空間だろう… || この工房はここの地名をとって月夜野窯というんだ || おじさんはここで粘土をこねたりろくろを回して仕事をしているんだ
english: Boku! This is my workshop. || Well? Quite an interesting space, isn't it? || This workshop is called the Tsukiyono Kiln, after the name of this place. || I work in here, kneading clay and turning the potter's wheel.

japanese: もう少し沢の方へ行ったところにある大きな焼き窯が登り窯っていうんだけど || あそこに一昼夜がんばって火を入れて焼き物を完成させるんだ
english: The big kiln a little farther down toward the creek is called a climbing kiln. || I keep a fire going in it for a whole day and night to finish the pottery.

japanese: え〜 じゃあボクがここにいる間に火を点けるってこともあるの？
english: Ooh! So might you light it while I'm still here?

japanese: う〜ん実はね、夏は窯に火を入れると暑いから、本当はやりたくないんだけどさ || 多分、八月の下旬になると焼くものが相当溜まってくるだろうから || その時には火を入れなきゃならないだろうなぁ
english: Hmmm. The truth is, firing the kiln in summer is hot, so I'd really rather not. || But by late August there'll probably be quite a pile of things to fire, || and I expect I'll have to light it then.

japanese: なんだか楽しみだね
english: I can't wait.

japanese: おじさんも暑い以外は楽しみなんだけどね
english: I'm looking forward to it too, apart from the heat.

japanese: な〜んだ、まだここにいたんだ || おじさんちは縁側の横に裏門があるんだけど || そこから橋を経由して山の方に出られるんだよ || 子供は大自然の中で遊んでいらっしゃい || 夜の山は危ないからあそこは昼間しか開けてないんだけどね
english: Oh, you're still here? || There's a back gate beside the veranda. || From there you can cross the bridge and get out to the mountains. || Kids should be off playing in the great outdoors. || The mountains are dangerous at night, though, so it's only open in the daytime.

japanese: 詩とデートしたのかい男の子はなにかと大変だな
english: So you went on a date with Shirabe? It's not easy being a boy.

japanese: おじさんも誰かとデートしたいなぁ…
english: I'd like to go on a date with somebody too...

japanese: あっ、おじちゃんの前に飛行機のプラモ！
english: Oh! There's a model airplane in front of you, Uncle!

japanese: うん！ || おじさんちの子がまだ、ちっちゃかった時に飛行機が大好きだったんだ || それで、おばちゃんが一生懸命組み立てたのさ
english: Yep! || When our child was still very small, he was crazy about airplanes. || So your aunt worked hard and put that together.

japanese: おじちゃんは作れないの？
english: Can't you build them, Uncle?

japanese: あはは、おじさんも作れるし作るのは好きだけど || こういうことはだいたいおばちゃんの担当なんだ
english: Ah ha ha. I can, and I like building them, || but that sort of thing is mostly your aunt's department.

japanese: おじちゃんはホタル見たことある？
english: Have you ever seen fireflies, Uncle?

japanese: うん、それに昔はそこら中で見られたからね
english: Sure. In the old days you could see them just about everywhere.

japanese: 納屋に古い斧をしまったけど || ボクくん、危ないから触っちゃだめだよ
english: I've put the old axe away in the shed. || It's dangerous, Boku, so don't touch it.

japanese: あ〜 筋肉痛だぁ
english: Ohh, my aching muscles.

japanese: 納屋に古い斧をしまったけど || ボクくん、危ないから触っちゃだめだよ
english: I've put the old axe away in the shed. || It's dangerous, Boku, so don't touch it.

japanese: なかなか面白いお坊さんだったろう
english: Quite a funny priest, wasn't he?

japanese: あのお坊さんああ見えても、もう六十近いんだよ
english: You'd never guess it, but that priest is nearly sixty.

japanese: ボクくん、おじさんの特製ブランコ… || もう乗ってみたかい？
english: Boku, my specially made swing... || Have you had a ride on it yet?

japanese: そうかい、じゃあ気をつけて乗るんだよ
english: Have you? Well, be careful on it.

japanese: へぇ…… まだなんだ || 面白いぞぉさぁ、早く乗ってきな
english: Oh...... Not yet? || It's fun! Go on, hurry up and try it.

japanese: 今年、おおかみ娘はお地蔵様を左に行った龍神池の近くに || テントを張っているらしいから会いに行ってみるといいよ
english: This year the Wolf Girl has apparently pitched her tent || near Ryujin Pond, left at the Jizo. You should go and see her.

japanese: ねぇ、森の中になんだか不思議な機械があるよ
english: Hey, there's a mysterious machine in the woods.

japanese: …不思議な機械？ || それは、どんな機械なのかな？
english: ...A mysterious machine? || What sort of machine is it?

japanese: ピカッ！ って光るんだ
english: It goes FLASH!

japanese: それは確かに不思議な機械だね
english: That certainly is a mysterious machine.

japanese: ボク、おおかみ娘に会ってきたよ
english: I went and met the Wolf Girl.

japanese: そうかい、なかなか面白い娘さんだろう？
english: Did you? Quite an interesting young lady, isn't she?

japanese: 面白い…… というか変なお姉ちゃん
english: Interesting...... More like a weird lady.

japanese: ははは、確かに
english: Ha ha ha, true enough.

japanese: ねぇ… ボクくんは将来どんな職業に就きたいと思う？
english: Say... what kind of job do you think you'd like to have someday, Boku?

japanese: え？ || ボクはね… || かんがえちゅう…
english: Huh? || Me? || Still thinking...

japanese: ボクくんて、将来どんな女の子と結婚するんだろうね？
english: I wonder what sort of girl you'll marry someday, Boku.

japanese: グラマラスな美人 / 財閥のご令嬢 / 年上の女性 /
english: A glamorous beauty || A tycoon's daughter || An older woman

japanese: 言葉の意味、わかってないと思うけど… 人間はやっぱり性格が大事だぞ！
english: I doubt you know what that means, but... it's personality that counts!

japanese: やっぱり、お金があるに越したことないのかな… || おじさん、お金持ちになったことがないから正直言ってわからないんだ
english: I suppose there's nothing better than having money... || I've never been rich, so honestly, I wouldn't know.

japanese: 実はおばちゃんっておじさんよりひとつ年上なんだ || 見合い結婚なのに籍を入れる直前まで年下だと信じていたんだ
english: As a matter of fact, your aunt is a year older than me. || It was an arranged marriage, and right up until we signed the papers I believed she was younger.

japanese: 猫とか犬とかタヌキとかいろ〜んなものをかぶっていたみたいで… || あっ！ 今のはおばちゃんに絶対内緒だよ
english: It seems she'd been putting on all sorts of acts. A cat, a dog, a tanuki, you name it... || Ah! That stays absolutely secret from your aunt!

japanese: もう、窯の準備終わったよ || 夕方になったら火を入れるからボクくんも見においで
english: The kiln's all ready. || I'll light it in the evening, so come and watch, Boku.

japanese: うん、楽しみだなぁ
english: Okay. I can't wait.

japanese: 今日の夜、窯を開けるから見においで || 宝の山がザックザクだよ！
english: I'm opening the kiln tonight, so come and see. || It'll be heaps and heaps of treasure!

japanese: あの写真、本当にニホンオオカミなのかな…
english: I wonder if that photo really is a Japanese wolf...

japanese: なんとなく、そう思っただけなんだけど… || なんか、もっと不思議で崇高な未知の存在が、この山にいるのかもしれないよ
english: It's only a feeling I have... || but there may be something even stranger, something sublime and unknown, on this mountain.

japanese: えっ？ おじちゃんなにか知っているの？
english: Huh? Do you know something, Uncle?

japanese: さぁ、どうだろうね…
english: Well now, I wonder...

japanese: ボクくん、今日の夜窯を開けるから見においで面白いぞぉ！
english: Boku, I'm opening the kiln tonight, so come and see. It'll be fun!

japanese: ねえおじちゃん
english: Hey, Uncle?

japanese: ん…… なんだい？
english: Mm...... What is it?

japanese: ろくろって目が回らないの？
english: Doesn't the potter's wheel make you dizzy?

japanese: あははは… さぁおじさんは回ったことがないけど、どうなのかな？
english: Ah ha ha ha... Well, I've never spun around on it myself, so who knows?

japanese: ろくろの回転を利用して大きなトンボを捕まえることは？
english: Could you use the spinning of the wheel to catch a big dragonfly?

japanese: できませ〜ん！
english: No, you cannooot!

japanese: ろくろを回してお茶碗をつくることを最初に考えた人って… || 実に柔軟な思考をもったすばらしい人だよね
english: Whoever first thought of spinning a wheel to make a bowl... || was a splendid person with a truly flexible mind.

japanese: え？ おじちゃんが発明したんじゃないんだ
english: Huh? So you didn't invent it, Uncle?

japanese: 凧を作ってもらいたい時は、居間の凧図鑑から欲しいものを選んでおいで
english: When you want a kite made, pick the one you want from the kite book in the living room.

japanese: 凧を作って欲しいようだけど、ごめんね || 今から作ってもボクくんがここにいる間には完成しないなぁ
english: It seems you'd like a kite made, but I'm sorry. || Even if I started now, it wouldn't be finished while you're here, Boku.

japanese: おめでとうボクくん！ || 高く高く上がった凧がこの庭からも見えていたよ || さあ、ご褒美に次の凧を作ってあげるから選んでおいで
english: Congratulations, Boku! || I could see your kite from this garden, way, way up high. || As a reward I'll make you the next kite, so go and choose one.

japanese: おじさんの凧がんばって高く上げてくれよ
english: Do your best and fly my kite nice and high.

japanese: おじさんの凧、もう少し高く上がる筈なんだけどな… || ここから見えるくらいに高く上げてくれたら、次を作ってあげるよ
english: That kite of mine ought to go a bit higher than that... || Fly it high enough to see from here, and I'll make you the next one.

japanese: 凧上げって難しいかい？とにかくもっともっと高く上げておくれ || そうしたら、この工房の窓からもきっと見える筈なんだから
english: Is kite flying hard? Anyway, get it up higher and higher. || Then I'm sure I'll be able to see it from the workshop window.

japanese: え、なになに…中張り角凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Square Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: 凧はまだ出来ていませ〜ん || もう、ちょっとだけ待ってて下さいね
english: The kite's not ready yeeet. || Please wait just a little longer.

japanese: ボクくん、凧、完成したよ
english: Boku, your kite is finished.

japanese: おじちゃんありがとう
english: Thanks, Uncle.

japanese: じゃあ目標はとりあえず || この家の庭から見えるくらいにその凧を高く高くお空に上げること
english: Now, your goal for the time being || is to fly that kite so high, high up in the sky that it can be seen from this garden.

japanese: うん、おじちゃん任しといて！ || ボク、がんばるよ
english: Okay, Uncle, leave it to me! || I'll do my best.

japanese: 角凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Square Kite.

japanese: え、なになに…にな凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Nina Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: にな凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Nina Kite.

japanese: え、なになに…せみ凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Cicada Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: せみ凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Cicada Kite.

japanese: え、なになに…とり凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Bird Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: とり凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Bird Kite.

japanese: この前渡した凧が最後のやつなんだから、がんばって高く上げてくれよ
english: The kite I gave you the other day is the last one, so do your best and fly it high.

japanese: え、なになに…こいのぼり凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Carp Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: こいのぼり凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Carp Kite.

japanese: え、なになに…ひこうき凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Airplane Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: ひこうき凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Airplane Kite.

japanese: 最後の難しい凧までちゃんと高く高く上げたんだね || ボクくん、もう凧上げはおじさんよりも数段うまいみたいだな || なんだかおじさんボクくんが頼もしく思えてきたよ
english: So you flew even that last, difficult kite way up high. || Boku, it looks like you're a good few notches better at kite flying than I am now. || I'm starting to think I can really count on you.

japanese: え、なになに…連凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Kite Train? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: 連凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Kite Train.

japanese: え、なになに…似顔絵凧 が欲しいのかい || よしよし… じゃあ二日ほど時間を下さいね
english: Hm? What's that... You'd like the Portrait Kite? || All right, all right... Give me about two days.

japanese: ボクくんこれが最後の凧だよやっと完成したんだ！
english: Boku, this is the last kite. It's finally finished!

japanese: 似顔絵凧を手に入れた
english: Got the Portrait Kite.

japanese: ボクくん、ちゃんと約束通りに来たね || じゃあ、窯の焚き口に火を入れるよ
english: Boku, you came just like you promised. || All right, I'm lighting the firebox.

japanese: この窯は… || 見た目の通り、斜面を登るように作られているから登り窯っていうんだ || この窯の形で下から火を焚くと熱が自然に斜面の上の方に昇っていくので || 中の温度を、効率良く千度以上まで上げることができるんだよ || だから、真夏にはあまり気の進まない暑〜い仕事なんだ
english: This kiln... || as you can see, is built climbing up the slope, so it's called a climbing kiln. || With this shape, when you light a fire at the bottom the heat rises up the slope by itself, || so you can bring the inside to over a thousand degrees very efficiently. || Which is why it's hot, hot work I'm never keen on in midsummer.

japanese: このあとはどうするの？
english: What happens after this?

japanese: まず、しばらくは三、四十分毎にたくさんの薪をくべるんだ || で、夜が明けた頃からそのペースを徐々に速くしていって
english: First, for a while, I feed in lots of firewood every thirty or forty minutes. || Then from around daybreak I gradually pick up the pace.

japanese: じゃあ、徹夜なんだ
english: So you stay up all night.

japanese: あはは、そりゃそうだよ || そして、そのあと明日の昼過ぎ頃に内部が目標の千二百度になったら || それを二時間ほどがんばって持続させて
english: Ah ha ha, of course I do. || Then sometime after noon tomorrow, when the inside reaches the target of twelve hundred degrees, || I work hard to hold it there for about two hours.

japanese: 夕方くらいにこの焚き口をふさいで火を消しちゃうんだ
english: And around evening I seal up this firebox and put the fire out.

japanese: それで完成？
english: And then it's done?

japanese: うん！ || でも、自然に冷めるのを待ってから窯を開けなきゃいけないから || 焼き上がったものとのご対面はあさっての夕方まで待っててね
english: Yep! || But I have to wait for it to cool by itself before opening the kiln, || so you'll have to wait until the evening of the day after tomorrow to meet the finished pieces.

japanese: ふぁ… 気の長い話だね
english: Fwah... That takes a lot of patience.

japanese: もう、お腹空いてきちゃったなぁ
english: I'm getting hungry already.

japanese: う〜ん、なかなかの出来栄えだぞ
english: Hmmm, these came out rather well.

japanese: つぎは、どんなイメージに挑戦しようかな？
english: What sort of image shall I take on next?

japanese: こおろぎの鳴き音に揺れし 我窯のまだ細き火に 我子抱かれん
english: Swaying to the song of crickets, in my kiln's still-slender flame, my child is held.

japanese: 明日、日が昇る頃になったら || 今より、もっとたくさんの薪が必要になるから || 今夜のうちにがんばって割っておかなきゃ…
english: Come sunrise tomorrow, || I'll need a lot more firewood than now, || so I'd better work hard and get it split tonight...

japanese: ねぇ、さっきの歌はどういう意味なの
english: Hey, what did that poem just now mean?

japanese: やっぱり夜になってくるとさすがにもう秋を感じるなぁ || って、感じかなぁ
english: Something like: once night comes on, you can't help feeling autumn's already here. || ...I suppose.

japanese: こら〜 ボクくんボクくんたら…
english: Heeey! Boku. Boku, I say...

japanese: この時間、ここから先は立ち入り禁止です || 暗くなって足元が見えないとユキノ川にドボンとはまるからね || これはおじさんちの決まりなんだから || …わかりましたか？
english: At this hour, it's off-limits from here on. || When it's dark and you can't see your feet, you'll go splash, right into the Yukino River. || That's the rule in this house. || ...Understood?

japanese: はい / いいえ / もう一回教えて？ /
english: Yes || No || Say that again?

japanese: よーし！ ものわかりの良い子だ、偉いぞ！
english: All right! You're a sensible boy. Good for you!

japanese: この家の名前は空野おじさんは優作っていうんだ || 今日からここを自分の家だと思って、たっぷり遊んでいって下さい
english: This family's name is Sorano. I'm Yusaku. || Starting today, think of this as your own home and play to your heart's content.

japanese: もえといいます || この家の長女ですよろしくね
english: My name is Moe. || I'm the eldest daughter. Nice to meet you.

japanese: わたしはしらべ詩って書いてしらべなの
english: I'm Shirabe. It's written "poem," and you say it Shirabe.

japanese: うちのおとうさんかっこいいでしょ || トーゲイカなんだお皿やお茶碗作るんだよ
english: Isn't my dad cool? || He's a pot-ter. He makes plates and bowls.

japanese: あなたのおとうさんの妹、薫おばちゃんですよろしくね
english: I'm your father's little sister, Aunt Kaoru. Nice to meet you.

japanese: なんだか、とてもお元気そうで… || というか、ど、どうしたんですか？
english: My, you're looking very well... || Or rather, wh-what's come over you?

japanese: わぁ！ おかあさん！ズルいてっばぁ
english: Waah! Mom! That's no faaair!

japanese: どうしたんだい？
english: What's the matter?

japanese: 今のところ、とりあえずだけど… || 私の愛すべき存在はおとうさんってことになっているの…
english: For the time being, at least... || the object of my affection is officially Dad...

japanese: とりあえずか… う〜ん || 娘を持った父親の悲しみここに至れり尽くせり…
english: For the time being... Hmmm. || Behold, the sorrows of a father with daughters, served with all the trimmings...

japanese: あら？ || おとうさんを恋人にするならここに強力なライバルがいるのをお忘れなく！
english: Oh? || If you plan to make your father your sweetheart, don't forget you have a powerful rival right here!

japanese: あらそう？ でも、私だって負けないんだから！
english: Oh, really? Well, I'm not going to lose!

japanese: あ〜あ、また明日がくるなぁ…
english: Sigh... Tomorrow's coming again...
